commit.message:
agentHost: diagnose missing model-call turn correlation (#335282)

* agentHost: diagnose missing model-call turn correlation

Record response correlation decisions and bounded late or rejected completion diagnostics. Identify sessions disposed during the correlation wait without changing turn attribution or the 100 ms deadline.

Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9110.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: slim model-call correlation diagnostics

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: isolate response telemetry correlation

Keep generic SDK telemetry forwarding free of response-specific session and turn-correlation handling. Cover direct forwarding without reading turn state.

commit.message:
agentHost: synchronize materialized worktree state (#335253)

* agentHost: synchronize materialized worktree state

Broadcast the resolved primary working directory to existing session subscribers and seed the generated worktree branch before publishing the materialized session. This keeps session state, catalogue summaries, and Agents window workspace presentation consistent.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: defer worktree reconciliation until turn completion

Commit the materialized worktree snapshot before publication, but delay the working-directory reconciliation action and full Git refresh until the active provider turn ends. This avoids forcing Claude to resume a provisional conversation during materialization while still converging existing clients afterward.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: discard stale git refresh results

Ignore Git state computed for a working directory that is no longer the session primary. Seed materialized worktrees with only repository-wide identity and base-branch metadata so provisional checkout state is not attributed to the new worktree.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: preserve materialization event ordering

Restore SessionAdded before SessionReady so existing provider snapshots remain stable, while retaining post-turn worktree reconciliation. Detect stale Git refreshes by comparing the session primary before and after the asynchronous query so explicit probe directories remain supported.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
remote: fix managed resource loading from workbench (#335241)

Chromium omits referrers for requests originating from the vscode-file
scheme because custom schemes are not registered as allowed referrer
sources. The protocol level referrer check therefore rejected every
legitimate managed remote resource request from the workbench.

Remove the unreliable referrer check and rely on the existing
webRequest frame tree validation, which rejects requests originating
from vscode-webview frames using browser owned frame identity.

Also return Buffer instances for error responses from the buffer
protocol handler. String response bodies are invalid for
registerBufferProtocol and caused intended HTTP error responses to
surface as net::ERR_FAILED.

Scope child discovery to the spawning chat, restore cross-client and nested subagent availability, and adopt completed client snapshots without duplicate pills. Keep cancelled tools from showing success labels and preserve synchronous setup for already-hydrated child chats.

* chat: always use collapsed preview thinking in read-only chats

Pass read-only state through the shared renderer and content context, overriding only the effective thinking style without changing user configuration. Rebuild reused templates when read-only state changes and apply the override consistently to grouping and completion. Cover all configured modes and editable/read-only transitions, and document the behavior in settings and accessibility help.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: suppress launch output in rich subagent headers

Remove the temporary Subagent output disclosure and its action-enabled listeners, preserve opt-out inline rendering, and cover live/restored launch acknowledgments and the inactive initialization gap.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: defer subagent entries and name completion notices

Publish subagent entries only after a child turn exists, appending them after intervening progress rather than reserving an early slot. Preserve observation and ordering across live, same-client, cross-client, and restored turns, and verify the full renderer in both themes.

Use the SDK display name or task description for live and restored background-agent completion notices instead of an opaque routing ID.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: distinguish agent titles in completion notices

* chat: break thinking at system completion notices

Finalize the current thinking group at a system notification and give subsequent parent reasoning a fresh protocol part. Keep running subagent reasoning independent and mount new collapsed tool groups after the boundary.

Cover live reasoning, replay, all thinking styles, read-only and incremental rendering, completed/remounted responses, and visible DOM ordering with full-renderer fixtures.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: follow list lifecycle in subagent fixtures

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Keep subagent launch metadata, deferred publication, and child observation alive with the session so children can start after their parent turn completes. Recover deferred idle history, route late progress to the original response, and honor catalog children for failed active-turn restores.

Keep provider-observed children visibly active until their own completion, and only mount newly split thinking-group roots so lazy edit markdown stays inside its collapsed group.

Add regressions for all contributor paths, delayed catalog recovery, original-response routing, disposal, failed restoration, and edit containment. Verified 865 tests and 16 CI-style component fixtures.

commit.message:
agentHost: route MCP auth during session initialization (#334593)

* agentHost: route MCP auth during session initialization

Track initializing Copilot sessions so host-supplied MCP tokens reach pending SDK authentication callbacks before live-session registration. Dispose tracked sessions during shutdown to unblock initialization.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: harden MCP auth initialization coverage

Centralize session initialization and registration so new call paths cannot bypass MCP auth routing. Exercise concurrent create, provisional materialization, default and peer resume, scope rejection, and shutdown through real CopilotAgent paths.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: deliver persisted MCP auth per session

Keep initializing sessions owned and routable until atomic registration, and scope silent MCP authentication coalescing to each session so later challenges receive their own token delivery. Add create, materialize, resume, peer, concurrency, and shutdown regression coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* agentHost: tighten MCP auth lifecycle identity

Use resource-aware session identity for silent auth coalescing and make the pre-registration lifecycle phase explicit.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Paul Wang <paulwang@Pauls-MacBook-Pro.local>
Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: back the checkpoint and fork rows over a chat background (#334985)

The Restore Checkpoint, Start Over and fork controls are transparent at
rest and only pick up a fill on hover, so over a chat background they read
straight on the wallpaper.

Back each row's toolbar and its sibling text with one opaque plate, the way
the editor-instance restore row already does in chat.css, rather than
plating each control. The controls stay transparent, so their existing
hover fill composites over the plate and the confirming Restore Checkpoint
pill keeps rendering as a single unit.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
sessions: Honor ignore files in text search (#335058)

* Sessions: Honor ignore files in text search

Register shared search settings in the common contribution so the Agents window receives the existing ignore-file and exclusion defaults without loading the Search view. Cover default queries and explicit overrides with regression tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Capture the common contribution schema before configuration suites reset the global registry, then create fresh per-test defaults without mutating global state. This also restricts coverage to settings registered by the common contribution.

commit.message:
fix: center the fork glyph in the chat checkpoint toolbar

The checkpoint toolbar renders the fork icon at the compact 12px size,
but the generic actionbar rule gives any descendant codicon a 16px flex
box with no horizontal alignment. The 12px glyph was left-aligned inside
that box, leaving the unused 4px on its right and shifting the icon ~2px
off-center inside an otherwise symmetric button.

Center the glyph within its icon box. Button size, padding, divider
lines, and Restore Checkpoint placement are unchanged, and the compact
loading spinner that reuses the same span is centered too.

Both the chat view and the Agents Window render this control through the
shared ChatForkActionViewItem, so a single scoped rule fixes both.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Fix terminal-editor shift-drop firing on detached instances (#318756)

Fix terminal-editor shift-drop firing on detached instances (#311164)

`TerminalInstance._dndObserver` was set by `_initDragAndDrop` but never
cleared by `detachFromElement`. A `TerminalEditor` pane reuses its
`_overflowGuardElement` across tab switches, so when one terminal was
detached and another attached to the same container, the old instance's
DragAndDropObserver was still listening on it. A shift+drop then fired
`sendPath` on every previously-attached terminal in that pane.

Disposing the observer on detach removes the listeners from the prior
container.

Fixes #311164

commit.message:
Fix `--no-proxy-server` command line argument being rejected (#313185)

* Initial plan

* Fix '--no-proxy-server' command line argument parsing

Minimist converts '--no-KEY' args by stripping the 'no-' prefix and
setting KEY=false. For '--no-proxy-server', this caused 'proxy-server'
to be set to false (boolean), which triggered the empty value error:
"Option 'proxy-server' requires a non empty value. Ignoring the option."

Fix: Pre-process args before passing to minimist. Any '--no-KEY' arg
where 'no-KEY' is a declared boolean option is extracted from the arg
list. After minimist runs, these are manually restored as true. This
prevents minimist from mangling the '--no-*' flags and also correctly
sets 'no-proxy-server=true' when '--no-proxy-server' is passed.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/199664

commit.message:
Fix customization migration hint shown on every request in 'once' mode (#335011)

fix: merge input state contrib instead of replacing it

chat.customizations.migrationHint: "once" showed the hint on every
request. ChatServiceImpl records that the hint was shown by writing a key
into the input model's `contrib` bag, but ChatInputPart.getCurrentInputState
rebuilds that bag from scratch and lets only widget contributions populate
it. The next input sync - typing, sending, or a model change - therefore
published a contrib object without the flag, and InputModel.setState
replaced the whole bag with it, so "once" degraded into "always".

setState takes a Partial<IChatModelInputState>, so a partial update must
not silently drop nested state it says nothing about. Merge contrib by key
so each writer owns its own keys.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Sort chat pill dropdown entries newest first (#334889)

* Sort chat pill dropdown entries newest first

Session artifacts and references are recorded by append, so their stored order runs oldest to newest. Every pill that lists them - artifacts, references, pull requests, issues, browsers and subagents - now shows the most recent entry at the top of its group.

Pull requests the session recorded also lead the ones discovered from its GitHub state on both the workbench and Agents Window surfaces, so the session's latest pull request is its active one.

Condense the inline comments added by the previous commit to a single line each.

Push matching views and reverse once, instead of unshifting each match and shifting the accumulated array on every recomputation.

commit.message:
Await session state before computing the customization migration hint (#334958)

* fix: await session state before computing migration hint

The customization migration hint reads migration destinations through
AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideSourceFolders, which resolves them
from a session-state subscription. IAgentSubscription.value is undefined
until its first snapshot arrives, and the workbench service collapses
that to an empty customization list.

Session-state subscriptions are keyed by chat UI resource. On the first
send of a new chat the untitled resource is materialized into a fresh
real resource, so a new subscription is created at that moment and its
first read yields no customizations. Every migration candidate is then
filtered out and no hint is shown, even though the same computation
reports the correct counts once the snapshot lands.

Add whenCustomizationsReady so one-shot callers can distinguish 'not
loaded yet' from 'no customizations', and await it in provideSourceFolders.
The wait is bounded and cancellable because the chat request path blocks
on the hint before sending the user's message.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Enhance documentation for whenCustomizationsReady method

Co-authored-by: Copilot Autofix powered by AI <175728472+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix: share one bounded readiness wait per session subscription

createFileMigration queries provideSourceFolders once per target prompt
type, sequentially, and computeMigrationHint runs categories covering
agent, instructions and skill candidates. With a per-call deadline a
subscription that never hydrates could therefore block the first message
for roughly three deadlines instead of one.

Memoize the wait on the session-state subscription entry so every
source-folder query behind a hint joins the same bounded wait. A new
subscription generation - including the untitled to real rebind that
backs a first send - starts with no memo, so that case still gets a full
wait. Each caller races the shared wait against its own token so one
cancellation cannot settle it for the others.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* docs: note the shared readiness deadline

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Keep Codex MCP tool progress out of the tool result (#334053)

* codex: keep MCP tool progress out of the tool result

The Codex mapper appended every mcpToolCall/progress message to the
entry's output and re-sent the whole concatenation as the content of a
ChatToolCallContentChanged action. That output field is what completion
falls back to, so when an MCP tool legitimately returned nothing the
progress narration was persisted as its result, an orphaned call's result
became the narration, and each notification resent an ever-growing string.

Progress now rides on _meta.progressMessage, a new IToolCallMeta key that
readToolCallMeta validates. The mapper records the _meta it emitted at
start on the tool call entry and spreads it into the progress action,
because the reducer replaces the whole bag whenever an action carries
one. Identical consecutive messages are coalesced. The mcpToolCall
completion no longer falls back to entry.output: nothing writes output for
that item type any more, and keeping the fallback would have left the one
path by which narration could still leak into the result.

On the workbench side, updateRunningToolSpecificData and
toolCallStateToInvocation surface the message through
ChatToolInvocation.acceptProgress while the call is Running, so a client
attaching mid-turn sees it as well. finalizeToolInvocation clears the
progress before didExecuteTool, which otherwise promotes any progress
message to pastTenseMessage whenever toolResultMessage is absent. The
adapter never sets toolResultMessage, so without the clear the last
progress string replaced the provider's past-tense text and became the
label for providers that omit one.

* chat: let an empty tool progress message clear the status line

`applyToolCallProgress` gated the call to `acceptProgress` on the message
being truthy, so an empty string was dropped. `progressMessage` is typed
and validated as any string, and Codex can send an empty message to clear
a status line it set earlier, so the invocation kept showing the stale
text instead. Both the running-refresh path and the mid-turn seeding path
go through this one helper, so both were affected; testing for undefined
instead fixes them together.

The mapper needed no change. It coalesces on

Keep Codex MCP tool progress out of the tool result (#334053)

* codex: keep MCP tool progress out of the tool result

The Codex mapper appended every mcpToolCall/progress message to the
entry's output and re-sent the whole concatenation as the content of a
ChatToolCallContentChanged action. That output field is what completion
falls back to, so when an MCP tool legitimately returned nothing the
progress narration was persisted as its result, an orphaned call's result
became the narration, and each notification resent an ever-growing string.

Progress now rides on _meta.progressMessage, a new IToolCallMeta key that
readToolCallMeta validates. The mapper records the _meta it emitted at
start on the tool call entry and spreads it into the progress action,
because the reducer replaces the whole bag whenever an action carries
one. Identical consecutive messages are coalesced. The mcpToolCall
completion no longer falls back to entry.output: nothing writes output for
that item type any more, and keeping the fallback would have left the one
path by which narration could still leak into the result.

On the workbench side, updateRunningToolSpecificData and
toolCallStateToInvocation surface the message through
ChatToolInvocation.acceptProgress while the call is Running, so a client
attaching mid-turn sees it as well. finalizeToolInvocation clears the
progress before didExecuteTool, which otherwise promotes any progress
message to pastTenseMessage whenever toolResultMessage is absent. The
adapter never sets toolResultMessage, so without the clear the last
progress string replaced the provider's past-tense text and became the
label for providers that omit one.

* chat: let an empty tool progress message clear the status line

`applyToolCallProgress` gated the call to `acceptProgress` on the message
being truthy, so an empty string was dropped. `progressMessage` is typed
and validated as any string, and Codex can send an empty message to clear
a status line it set earlier, so the invocation kept showing the stale
text instead. Both the running-refresh path and the mid-turn seeding path
go through this one helper, so both were affected; testing for undefined
instead fixes them together.

The mapper needed no change. It coalesces on
`params.message === entry.progressMessage`, and the entry's
`progressMessage` starts undefined rather than empty, so a first empty
message is a real change and still emits; only a repeat of the same empty
message is dropped.

commit.message:
Center full-width characters in two monospace cells (#334022)

* Center full-width characters in two monospace cells

Adds `editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth`, which renders every full-width
character inside a box exactly two character cells wide, so CJK text lines
up with the surrounding narrow characters on a monospace grid.

The renderer splits each full-width character into a part of its own and
gives that part a fixed-width, centered inline-block. Characters that begin
a longer grapheme cluster are skipped so the cluster is never torn apart.

Adds the computed option `effectiveForceFullwidthCharacterWidth`, which
turns the setting off when the font is not monospace.

Closes #155588

commit.message:
Fix primary side bar width reset when toggled (#334167)

`SplitView.onViewChange` redistributed the size a view gained or gave up in
plain index order, unlike `resizeView` which is layout priority aware. With
Modern UI and the primary side bar on the right, the activity bar changes its
fixed width with side bar visibility and reports that change re-entrantly from
`Part.setVisible`, while `setViewVisible` is still restoring the side bar to
its cached size. Index order made the side bar the first candidate, so it was
squeezed to its minimum width on every toggle. On the left the flexible editor
happened to come first, which is why only the right side showed the bug.

Redistribute by layout priority instead, so the high priority editor absorbs
the change.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
automations: refactor: make provider session templates canonical (#334521)

* automations: fix: preserve legacy Autopilot mode mapping

Translate legacy Autopilot permission selections into separate Agent Host Mode and Assisted approvals, preserving explicit Plan mode. Do not forward generic workbench chat modes into Agent Host session configuration.

Keep the Automation projection and its regressions separate from runtime approval-policy enforcement.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* agentHost: fix: revalidate Copilot approvals against policy

Resolve supplied elevated approval preferences against the current root policy before validating Copilot session configuration. Restrict approvals to default without changing the independently selected execution mode.

Cover a policy change between configuration resolutions so a stored Assisted preference cannot bypass a newly applied restriction.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: harden legacy Autopilot migration

Preserve provider-owned configuration across compatibility edits, repair existing and provider-less Copilot Automation definitions, and reset incompatible state on retargeting. Enforce managed auto-approval policy at both SDK and host decision points while keeping saved preferences intact.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: preserve provider session templates

Add a versioned provider-neutral session template projection for model, agent, and opaque configuration. Keep legacy flat writers functional during migration, preserve unknown AHP state on edits and transfers, and clear incompatible configuration on retarget.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: restore provider draft configuration

Let Automation drafts restore and capture provider-owned model, agent, and resolved configuration through the Sessions provider contract. Keep normal New Session defaults isolated, reject replaced draft snapshots, and exclude transient or target-owned values.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: reuse provider session controls

Drive Automation configuration through a scoped session draft and the same provider-owned pickers as New Session. Capture complete provider state for Agent Host and legacy Copilot paths while preserving unavailable, opaque, removed, and policy-clamped preferences.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: unify fallback session configuration

Pass the complete provider-owned Automation configuration during older-host draft creation so browser fallback and AHP execution use the same template semantics. Keep workspace isolation and branch configuration target-owned.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: expose canonical provider configuration

Round-trip complete provider session templates through Automation tools and stop new dialog and AHP projections from writing flattened aliases. Keep legacy rows and inputs compatible while enforcing template-first execution, duplication, telemetry, and rollback semantics.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: test: validate config after host restart

Specify canonical Automation template and draft ownership across Sessions and Agent Host. Add recorded AHP coverage proving independent Mode and Approvals survive host restart into the created run session, and document the remaining Claude/Codex coverage gap.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: harden provider configuration handling

Keep canonical provider templates opaque and authoritative while limiting legacy Autopilot repair to load/import boundaries. Bound dialog capture and preserve per-target configuration across failures and retargeting, retain legacy duplicate/worktree settings, and improve loading accessibility. Add regression coverage for #333723 compatibility, canonical reloads, capture races, and tool configuration limits.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: make configuration saving failure-safe

Keep the Automation dialog open when provider configuration cannot be captured, expose cancellable saving progress, and serialize draft retargeting. Unify canonical-template authority across stores, require providers to advertise restoration support, preserve definition-owned state, retain scoped picker models across toolbar rebuilds, and keep legacy fallback configuration available.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: normalize provider handoff and saving focus

Send providers one canonical Automation configuration object instead of overlapping template channels. Keep keyboard focus on the cancellable action while form content is inert, and make saving and error live regions visible before their announcements change.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: test: assert settled restart configuration

Refresh the created run session inside the completion retry so the restart E2E validates Mode and Approvals on the settled session rather than an earlier catalog snapshot.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: skip disabled actions in dialog focus

Exclude aria-disabled controls from the Automation dialog's custom focus ring so Saving keeps keyboard focus on the cancellable action instead of moving onto the disabled primary button.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: refactor: keep async dialog lifecycle local

Avoid extending the widely shared Dialog widget for the Automation editor's provider capture flow. Keep Save failure handling, cancellation, and completion in the Automation dialog while reusing the standard button styles and platform order.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: address canonical template review feedback

Filter reserved session state at both Agent Host projection and fallback restoration, preserve configuration for unavailable targets, honor explicit template reset semantics, and keep the Automation prompt menu owned by Sessions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: reject unresolved configuration capture

Wait for tracked configuration operations before capturing Automation state. Retry failed host resolution strictly with the attempted values so a transient failure cannot erase explicitly changed preferences.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: scope fallback agent pickers to their session

Reuse the existing scope-owned Mode picker cache for both provider families. Automation controls now discover and display their own agents rather than the active session, with regression coverage for scope isolation, toolbar rebuilds, retargeting, and disposal.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: restore fallback agents before sending

Restore canonical custom-agent URIs and capture the current selection instead of copying the initial agent. Refresh custom-mode discovery before the first Automation request, including cached selections, and fail explicitly if the agent is unavailable. Cancel discovery when the draft is discarded and reject unsupported cloud agent templates.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: bound fallback custom-agent discovery

Limit custom-agent resolution to one 30-second deadline across selection changes. Dispose each discovery scope and cancel its wait on timeout or draft/provider disposal, rather than retaining hung discovery during recurring Automation runs.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: preserve model-specific run configuration

Live verification showed Codex running at Medium despite a saved Low thinking selection. Capture model preferences in provider-owned drafts and preserve them through tools, persistence, AHP projection, and fallback requests without rewriting shared defaults on restore.

Carry the full model onto the first Automation message so completed runs restore their actual configuration. Refresh same-model configuration badges when switching draft targets, and cover capture, isolation, reset, validation, and restoration with regressions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

* automations: fix: use dot notation in template parsing

The PR merge build enables the bracket-notation lint rule added on main after this branch was based. Replace the four literal property accesses flagged by CI without changing parsing behavior.

Validated the exact rule with zero warnings and all 34 Automation tool tests against fresh output.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>
Copilot-Session: 09e55c0c-bf80-42ea-b8e2-fad38a12d986

commit.message:
mcp: validate gallery server sources and package types (#334761)

* mcp: validate gallery server sources and package types

Validate gallery server URLs before issuing requests and disable redirect following for server-document fetches. Reject unknown registry values before command construction while preserving usable package and remote entries across supported manifest schemas, including the Copilot NuGet mapping path.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: reuse package filtering logic

Extract the repeated registry normalization and package filtering loops in the core and Copilot manifest serializers. Restore command resolution to its original construction site while retaining fail-closed handling for unsupported registry types.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* request: avoid injecting fetch implementation

Keep redirect handling in the shared request implementation without extending its public function signature. Remove the dedicated fetch injection test while retaining MCP service-level redirect coverage.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: parse compatibility gallery entries independently

Avoid selecting one serializer for an entire compatibility page based on a single entry. Parse each server through the shape-aware dispatcher and normalize both cursor spellings so malformed records cannot hide or truncate valid results.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: restrict gallery server fetches to HTTP

Reject opaque-origin and custom-scheme server document URLs before network access. Direct gallery server fetches now require HTTP or HTTPS in addition to matching the configured gallery origin and path.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: handle optional gallery count metadata

Accept compatibility gallery pages that omit optional count metadata while retaining validation for invalid supplied values. Add direct Electron request coverage proving that followRedirects zero returns an opaque redirect without requesting the target.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization (#334696)

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub
items, falling back to standard options. Telemetry from experiment f716301b
showed 61% of impressions timed out with zero GitHub options, and the existing
events could not measure partial success: `fallbackReason` was only 'none' when
all 3 slots were GitHub, so 2 real issues logged identically to zero.

Telemetry (additive; existing field names and values unchanged):
- promptStrategy gains gitHubOptionCount, candidatesFound, lookupDurationMs,
  per-stage durations and outcomes, and timedOutStage.
- promptOptionInteraction gains optionIndex and optionKindsShown, so per-option
  CTR is computable rather than confounded with availability.
- Both gain a shared impressionId, replacing lossy DevDeviceId joins.
- New 'noComposer' fallback reason splits the infra-bug meaning out of the
  overloaded 'noCandidate'.
- Bounded categories and counts only: no titles, URLs, numbers, repository
  names or prompt text.

Latency, without raising the 10s total budget:
- Publish issue candidates before the linkage lookup, which only filters out
  issues that already have linked pull requests and so must never hide them.
- Keep review-thread enrichment off the critical path; it produced the least
  picked option while being the most expensive stage.
- Rebalance sub-budgets to 4000/1500/3000 so the concurrent chains fit.
- Stream options into the composer: paint the standard options immediately and
  replace slots as lookups land, instead of blocking first paint on the lookup.

INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve gains an optional progress callback
that reports whether an update was rendered, so the composer can refuse late
updates while the user is acting on the options and telemetry still describes
what was actually shown.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agentHost: publish client tools before starting turns (#334385)

* agentHost: publish client tools before starting turns

Flush and await the latest active-client snapshot before dispatching new or resumed turns so tools registered during MCP startup are available on the first provider request. Keep the barrier cancellation-aware and cover ordering and cancellation regressions.

* agentHost: harden active client turn barrier

Avoid retaining cancelled unresolved claims and reconcile before reading resumed-turn state so concurrent resumes are joined instead of duplicated. Strengthen both race regressions.

commit.message:
chat: fix GitHub context repository selection (#334594)

* chat: fix GitHub context repository selection

Avoid waiting for unresolved local Git metadata in the Agents window, and initialize every workspace root before choosing a repository in multi-root editor windows.\n\nFixes #334563\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: preserve workspace folder choices for GitHub context

Keep multi-root workspace folders as distinct Issue and Pull Request picker entries, even when they resolve to the same GitHub repository.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: choose workspace folder before GitHub context

Show multi-root workspace folders before resolving GitHub metadata so Issue and Pull Request attachment never skips folder selection while repository state is still loading.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: avoid blocking GitHub context repository discovery

Build multi-root choices from workspace folders and already-known repositories so unresolved Git state cannot prevent the Issue or Pull Request picker from opening.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: scope GitHub context to selected folder

Pass unresolved workspace folder selections to Copilot Chat and resolve their remotes without waiting for repository HEAD state. This keeps issue and pull request searches limited to the chosen repository even while Git discovery is incomplete.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: resolve Git worktree remotes for context

Follow Git worktree directory pointers and common directories when resolving the selected folder's remote. Preserve normal remote preference ordering so origin is chosen consistently when repository discovery is unavailable.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: use selected Agents folder for GitHub context

Pass a single selected local folder directly to Issue and Pull Request attachment commands. Only offer repository selection when that folder cannot be resolved.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: fix GitHub repository picker typing

Make the repository quick pick explicitly single-select and pass a mutable pick array so Compile & Hygiene resolves the correct overload.\n\nCo-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Fix Copilot session provider formatting

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
Leave agent host session state events unchanged

The MCP migration editor does not need a working-directory event of its
own. Workspace-folder MCP servers are client-forwarded, so adding or
removing a root republishes the active client's customization set and
the existing customizations event already fires. A root carrying no
customizations contributes no migration candidates either, so the list
stays correct without it.

commit.message:
Use session working directories for MCP migration

Planning and execution read different root sets: candidates came from
getWorkingDirectories while writes required server-confirmed roots. For
a provisional session those disagree, so the editor listed migratable
servers and then failed every one as no longer eligible.

Both paths now use getWorkingDirectories, which removes the need for a
separate verified accessor on the agent host providers and customization
services. The file-level guards in the migrator, which re-derive the
target from the source path and revalidate contents before and after
each write, remain the protection against acting on stale state.

dictation: fix indefinite hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls (#334526)

Fix dictation hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls

The on-device (nemo/Foundry Local) dictation backend awaited several
native SDK calls with no timeout and no AbortSignal: the model catalog
lookup, model.load(), session.start(), each session.append() call
(chained serially so one stuck append blocks every later chunk and
stop()), the result stream's next(), and session.stop()/dispose().

If any of these stalls (proxy/firewall silently dropping packets, a
wedged native addon, a driver hiccup during model load), the awaiting
promise never settles. Since start()/pushAudio()/stop()/cancel() all
await these calls directly or transitively, dictation would hang
indefinitely with no error surfaced to the user and no way to recover
short of restarting VS Code.

Guard each of these awaits with a hard timeout that rejects with a
descriptive error, mirroring the existing inactivity-timeout pattern
already used for the native runtime tarball download. A timeout now
surfaces as a normal model/session Error (with a new 'timeout' error
code from classifyModelError) so the existing error-handling UI path
picks it up, and Stop/Cancel can no longer hang forever.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

pull_requests.title: docs: remove obsolete "larger than three" from TextEditor.viewColumn
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335331

### Description
In `src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts`, the JSDoc for `TextEditor.viewColumn` states:
```typescript
/**
 * The column in which this editor shows. Will be `undefined` in case this
 * isn't one of the main editors, e.g. an embedded editor, or when the editor
 * column is larger than three.
 */
readonly viewColumn: ViewColumn | undefined;
```

The clause `"or when the editor column is larger than three"` is outdated legacy text from May 2018 (PR #49599) when `ViewColumn` only defined values up to `Three`. 

As verified in #52315, `textEditor.viewColumn` is defined for any column in the grid layout, and `ViewColumn.to(position)` converts any `EditorGroupColumn >= 0` to a `ViewColumn`. `viewColumn` is only `undefined` when the editor is not placed in a main editor group (e.g. embedded editors in Peek Views, inline widgets).

This PR removes the obsolete phrase.

pull_requests.title: Terminal: tolerate float error when scaling charHeight to device pixels
pull_requests.body:
`getXtermScaledDimensions` ceils `font.charHeight * devicePixelRatio`. `charHeight` is xterm's device cell height divided by `devicePixelRatio` (`getFont` reads `renderService.dimensions.css.cell`), so the product can land a few ulps above the whole pixel and ceil adds a device pixel per row.

At `window.zoomLevel: 1` (ratio 1.2) with a 22 px cell, `22 / 1.2 * 1.2` is `22.000000000000004`, so rows are computed with 23 px. A 1257 px tall terminal editor gets 54 rows instead of 57, and since the grid is bottom-anchored the three missing rows appear as blank space above the first line. 25 px and 28 px cells hit the same case.

Fix: subtract a small tolerance before the ceil. Fractional device heights (e.g. 17 * 1.2 = 20.4) still round up.

Adds unit tests for both cases.

pull_requests.title: automations: fix: keep popup Escape from closing the dialog
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334869.

## Problem

Escape should dismiss an Automation picker and leave the modal and unsaved form intact. The custom SelectBox closes on keydown and returns focus to its select, whereas the generic Dialog closes on keyup.

The existing Automations keyboard guard cleared popup ownership on every keydown outside a popup and every unrelated keyup. Holding Escape therefore produced this sequence:

1. Escape keydown targets the popup and enables suppression.
2. The popup closes and restores focus to the select.
3. Repeated Escape keydown targets the form and clears suppression.
4. Escape keyup reaches Dialog and closes the modal too.

Interleaved keydown/keyup events can cause the same failure. An ordinary `keyboard.press("Escape")` passes on the original code; repeated keydowns reliably reproduce the double dismissal.

## Fix

Establish popup ownership on the initial, non-repeated Escape keydown and retain it until Escape keyup. Ignore repeat and unrelated key events when updating that ownership. A fresh independent Escape press still closes the dialog.

The change stays in the Automations keyboard helper. Shared Dialog and SelectBox implementations, popup detection, focus trapping, listener registration/disposal, and native-picker selection are unchanged.

## Regression coverage

Four composed tests use real Dialog, SelectBox and ContextViewHandler instances, with the production listener registration order and events dispatched to the actual focused element. They cover normal Escape, key repeat, interleaved keydown and interleaved keyup. Each verifies popup dismissal, focus restoration, preserved selection and dismissal by a subsequent independent Escape.

Three new regression cases fail against the original helper.

## Validation

- 51 tests pass across Automation dialog, Dialog and SelectBox suites.
- Changed-file ESLint, whitespace checks and commit hygiene pass.
- Live macOS Agents-window checks reproduce the failure before the fix and pass afterward for Schedule repeat/interleaved keys, Time repeat and Day repeat. They also verify unsaved name preservation and normal subsequent dismissal.
- A live held-Escape check also passes for the workspace action popup.

Native OS pickers, Windows/Linux, screen readers and physical keyboard timing were not certified by this validation.

### What changed this cycle

- No product/build, `.vscodeignore`, `.moduleignore`, `copilot.ts`, version-pin,
  lockfile, or `*.traffic.ahp.yaml` changes were needed or made.

### Verdict / insight that drove it
- **Authoritative failure:** the Linux / Electron PR check (run
  [34379439009](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/34379439009/job/102560346409))
  reported **19 failing** tests, all `Agent Host E2E — Copilot prompts` →

- **Root cause (API/contract change, not a regression):** the `@github/copilot`

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Long-lived feedback annotation subscriptions were keeping entire conversations resident. Once those sessions exhausted the MRU budget, a newly completed session could be evicted as soon as its chat closed, making reopening it require a slow provider restore.

- Keep annotation subscriptions synchronized without treating them as conversation residency holds or MRU activity.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: diagnose missing model-call turn correlation
pull_requests.body:
add some diagnostic information to the response telemetry to collect more information about missing turn IDs.

## What is changing

Make missing Copilot Agent Host model-call-to-turn correlation diagnosable without filling in guessed turn IDs.

Missing `turnId` currently conflates unknown sessions, unavailable active turns, expired correlation waits, and lifecycle/routing losses. This adds a small set of fields to the existing `copilotSdk/response.success` and `response.error` events; it adds no new event type, hashed identifier, or diagnostic retention cache.

For example, deleting a streaming session can now be identified as `waitExpired` with `ahSessionDisposedDuringWait = true`, rather than appearing as an unexplained missing turn.

Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9110. This adds diagnostics; it does not fix the attribution loss or change the scorecard. The 100 ms deadline and existing turn-attribution behavior are preserved.

The generic forwarding path only dispatches by event kind. Session lookup, turn correlation, and diagnostics are isolated in `_forwardResponseTelemetry`; non-response events forward directly without reading turn-correlation state.

## Fields

- `ahCorrelationOutcome`: the host correlation decision, including a distinction between actual wait expiry and an already-forwarded short-circuit.
- `ahCorrelationWaitMs`: actual elapsed wait, only when a wait occurred.
- `ahActiveRootTurnIdAtResponse`: the active root turn captured at callback entry, only when final attribution is missing and a root turn was active.
- `ahSessionDisposedDuringWait`: whether the session was disposed by the end of the wait, only when a wait occurred and final attribution is missing.

`ahActiveRootTurnIdAtResponse` is contextual information, not an attribution repair. A subagent shares the root SDK session, and a late response may arrive during a different root turn. Do not coalesce this field into `turnId` or use it to assign model time to that turn.

Responses with a populated host `turnId` carry only the outcome and, where applicable, wait duration. Missing-attribution diagnostics apply to both `response.success` and `response.error`: a successful model response can still lack turn attribution. The fields distinguish failure categories but do not establish whether an unavailable completion was delayed, rejected, or never produced.

## Local runtime evidence

Exercised real OSS workflows with root tool loops, parallel subagents, cancellation/recovery, steering, and deletion near the final response.

- Normal delivery: 53 agent-initiated waits had a 4.10 ms median and 6.36 ms maximum, with no missing correlations.
- Lifecycle investigation reproduced a response arriving with a known session and active turn, followed by disposal 79.96 ms later. No completion callback was observed; the wait expired after 102.49 ms and forwarding omitted the turn.
- Before slimming the diagnostics to these fields, a subsequent run without temporary probes emitted `mappingWaited` at 4.50 ms for a normal response and `waitExpired` at 109.61 ms with the disposal flag set for a deleted streaming session. Successful response turn IDs matched host turn telemetry.

pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests

## Summary

Fix Agents Window sessions remaining `Working...` after a retained Copilot subagent finishes a follow-up.

The SDK can finish a `subagentStop` hook before delivering the final assistant messages. Previously, the adapter completed the child at the hook, then interpreted those trailing messages as new work and reopened an empty turn. Delayed completion hooks could also affect a newer follow-up.

This change makes completion terminal for each invocation instead of inferring activity from response events:

- Track explicit pending, running, and completed invocations. Only genuine request/start boundaries create new invocations.
- Bind stop hooks and SDK loop boundaries to their originating invocation, and drain final response events before normal completion.
- Keep identifiable late messages, reasoning, tool updates, and usage out of newer invocations, including legacy usage routing.
- Preserve genuine follow-ups, reused or missing interaction IDs, stop-hook continuation, errors, cancellation, and per-invocation accounting.

The sidebar's status aggregation is unchanged; the fix is in the provider state it consumes. Follow-up to #334781.

## Validation

- 653 tests passed across `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` and `agentSideEffects.test.ts`.
- Targeted TypeScript diagnostics and ESLint passed for both changed files.
- Regression coverage includes the observed stop-hook/final-message ordering, late response events, stale completion hooks, reused loop IDs, genuine follow-ups, and cancellation.

## How to test

Run the provider and host-routing suites after transpiling:

```sh
npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts
```

For manual verification, run a Copilot session in the Agents Window that creates a reusable subagent and sends it a follow-up. After both the main agent and child finish, confirm that the child's final response remains visible and the session no longer shows `Working...`. Send another follow-up and confirm that it starts and finishes normally.

pull_requests.title: sessions: restore Codex threads across clients
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Codex threads created in another client could fail to open in VS Code when the other client held the native writer lock or the saved model was unavailable to VS Code's bundled app-server. Lazy discovery could also leave imported sessions listed with placeholder titles.

- Read thread metadata and history without eagerly resuming the thread. Defer writer ownership and missing-rollout recovery until the first send.
- Resolve unavailable saved models to an available model from the **same provider**, waiting for queued model discovery and dropping incompatible saved model configuration. Keep the saved selection if that provider has no available models, so history remains readable.
- Supply both the selected model and provider on resume. Keep restored metadata, runtime, and subsequent sends aligned while preserving historical model attribution.
- Prevent a display-only model-picker fallback from overriding an existing Agent Host conversation's intended selection or switching billing providers.
- Refresh hydrated session titles in place, preserving custom titles and recency without materializing the conversation.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client` — passed.
- `npm run precommit` — passed for all staged changes, including the normal commit hook.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Codex unit suite — **430 passing**.
- AgentService unit suite — **411 passing**, 16 existing pending.
- ChatWidget unit suite — **22 passing**.
- Live Code OSS verification: an imported thread is discoverable and opens with the bundled Codex **0.149.1**, with no SDK override. The model picker, native runtime, and outgoing request options agree on an available model from the original provider.

## Reviewer Notes

No Codex dependency update or SDK override is required. Native single-writer restrictions still apply when sending from another client. Live verification only read the original thread; first-send continuation and fallback behavior are covered by regression tests rather than sending a new message to that conversation.

pull_requests.title: remote: fix managed resource loading from workbench
pull_requests.body:
Chromium omits referrers for requests originating from the vscode-file scheme because custom schemes are not registered as allowed referrer sources. The protocol level referrer check therefore rejected every legitimate managed remote resource request from the workbench.

Remove the unreliable referrer check and rely on the existing webRequest frame tree validation, which rejects requests originating from vscode-webview frames using browser owned frame identity.

Also return Buffer instances for error responses from the buffer protocol handler. String response bodies are invalid for registerBufferProtocol and caused intended HTTP error responses to surface as net::ERR_FAILED.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334144

pull_requests.title: agentHost: Add macOS Docker PATH fallback
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Append `/usr/local/bin` to the Dev Container shell environment on macOS when absent, matching the existing Dev Containers workaround from microsoft/vscode-remote-release#5396.
- Apply the fallback after both successful shell resolution and timeout/error recovery, so Docker availability checks and container launches use the same corrected PATH.
- Preserve existing PATH precedence, avoid duplicate entries, handle empty/missing PATH without adding the current directory, and leave Linux/Windows unchanged.
- Copy the environment instead of modifying `process.env`; retain shell-resolution error logging and trace when the fallback is applied.

## Why

During a multi-window macOS startup, the shared-process shell probe can exceed the configured timeout. The inherited GUI environment may then contain only `/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin`, so Docker installed under `/usr/local/bin` is not discovered and the New Session Dev Container checkbox disappears. A later shell result cannot recover the already-rejected cached promise.

This fixes Docker discovery independently of shell startup latency; it does not change shell timeouts, retry behavior, or feature gates.

pull_requests.title: git: detect corrupt index and provide recovery action
pull_requests.body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to VS Code! -->

### Why
On Windows, interrupted writes or process crashes (e.g. from background tasks or external tools) can truncate `.git/index` to 0 bytes. Git then fails with:
`fatal: .git/index: index file smaller than expected`

Previously, VS Code showed repeated blocking modal errors on commands, while background file-watcher refreshes failed silently without offering any way to recover.

### What
- **Error classification**: Added `GitErrorCodes.IndexCorrupted` matching corrupt/truncated index errors (`index file smaller than expected`, `index file corrupt`, `bad index file`, `error: bad signature`) in `git.ts`, `git.d.ts`, and `git.constants.ts`.
- **Transient retry**: Added a 3-attempt quadratic backoff retry in `Repository.updateModelState()` with an isolated cancellation token source, cancellation exit checks, and proper token disposal so in-flight external writes can finish without leaking stale updates.
- **Safe index rebuild**: Added `rebuildIndex()` which:
  - Validates `.git/index.lock` both prior to reset and before swapping to prevent collisions with active or concurrent Git processes.
  - Revalidates index health with `git status --porcelain` to preserve staged files if the index was already repaired.
  - Generates a unique temporary index path per attempt (`index.rebuild-${Date.now()}-${random}`) via `GIT_INDEX_FILE` so stale files from prior interrupted runs never block future recovery.
  - Atomically swaps in the replacement index via `fsPromises.rename` (cleaning up in `finally`), guaranteeing the repository is never stranded without an index if reset fails.
  - Safely handles unborn branches without `HEAD`.
- **Recovery action**: Shows a non-modal warning notification with a localized **Rebuild Index** button on both user commands and background watcher refreshes.
- **Target resolution**: Preserves the failing repository reference on errors so multi-root workspaces always rebuild the correct repository.
- **Unit tests**: Added classification tests for index corruption messages in `git.test.ts`.

### How to test
1. Open a Git repository in VS Code with some uncommitted changes.
2. Truncate `.git/index` to 0 bytes:
   ```sh
   > .git/index
   ```
3. Trigger a Git operation or wait for the background refresh:
   - A warning notification appears: *"The Git index file (.git/index) is corrupted. Would you like to rebuild it?"*
4. Click **Rebuild Index**:
   - The index is rebuilt cleanly.
   - Working tree changes remain intact and Git status returns to normal.

pull_requests.title: Acquire a process lock on the session data directory
pull_requests.body:
@deepak1556 

The main IPC handle is scoped to the product version, so right after an update the new process fails to detect the old one via claimInstance and both processes end up using the same user data directory at the same time. Chromium does not support sharing session data between multiple running browser processes and webview service worker registration then fails with an InvalidStateError.

Add a version independent process lock for the session data:

- createStaticIPCHandle now allows omitting the version so that the same handle is produced by all versions for a given user data directory (existing callers are unchanged)
- the main process serves that handle (environmentMainService. sessionDataLockHandle) for its whole lifetime before any storage in the user data directory is opened (claimSessionData runs right after claimInstance and before initServices)
- if a live lock holder exists, the process waits for it to exit (polling every second, dialog after 10s with Keep Waiting/Exit that re-appears every 60s), because concurrent use of the session data directory is unsupported and can corrupt Chromium state storage
- stale sockets of dead processes are recovered by probing the handle and unlinking it, mirroring claimInstance; the lock is released on shutdown

---

Previous MR: [https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333833](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333833)
Related Issue: [https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/125993](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/125993)

pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335000

Windows setup detection currently requires `unins000.exe` beside the executable. Inno Setup can legitimately generate a different numbered uninstaller, such as `unins001.exe`. This incorrectly classifies an official User Setup installation as an archive, selects the ZIP update feed, and opens the download in a browser instead of installing it.

- Detect Setup installations from the installer-generated `product.target` values `user` and `system`; missing or unexpected targets remain Archive.
- Use the same detection for update classification and both installer-mutex checks.
- Remove the filesystem probe and unnecessary process-global update-type cache.
- Add regression coverage for User/System Setup and missing or unexpected targets. Genuine ZIP installations retain manual updates.

pull_requests.title: fix: derive synced customization nonce from file content (build fix for vscode-engineering#3814)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The Electron unit-test job failed on `main` with one deterministic failing test in `SyncedCustomizationBundler`:

```
1) SyncedCustomizationBundler
     bundles complete SKILL.md directories:
  AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: Expected "actual" to be strictly unequal to: '737882158'
      at syncedCustomizationBundler.test.js:200:12
```

The assertion `assert.notStrictEqual(updatedResult!.ref.nonce, result.ref.nonce)` expects the bundle nonce to change after a reference file inside a skill directory is edited, but the recomputed nonce was identical. The two subsequent macOS-stage failures (non-production check and Publish Log Files, both reporting a missing `.build/logs`) are cascades of the test job aborting.

## Root cause

`SyncedCustomizationBundler._bundle` computed its change-detection nonce purely from file metadata:

```ts
entries.push({ ..., hashPart: `${hashKey}:${source.mtime}:${source.size}` });
```

The nonce therefore only reflects each file's `mtime` and `size`. When a file's content is edited to the same byte length within the filesystem's `mtime` resolution — as in the regression test, where `references/notes.md` changes from `reference content` (17 bytes) to `updated reference` (17 bytes) and the in-memory provider stamps both writes with the same `Date.now()` millisecond — the metadata is unchanged, so the nonce collides. The bundler then hits its "nothing changed" fast path and reuses the previous bundle, silently dropping the real content change from downstream agent-host syncs. This is a deterministic correctness bug, not a flake.

## How the fix works

The nonce is now derived from actual file content instead of metadata. File contents are read before the nonce is computed, and each file contributes a length-sensitive content hash (`hashBytes`) to the nonce inputs. A same-size content edit now produces a different hash, so the nonce changes and the bundle is correctly rewritten and re-synced. The metadata (`mtime`/`size`) is no longer part of the nonce. The write-skip optimization is preserved: the fast path still short-circuits when the content-based nonce is unchanged. Reading contents up front is not extra work — the previous code already read every file's contents immediately afterward to write the plugin tree; only the ordering relative to the nonce check moved.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Public culprit: `400640316376fbbdc6e901a7f5c23810bd5a9329` (#334568) added the regression test that exposes this pre-existing metadata-only nonce; the nonce logic itself predates it (introduced in #333827, `42b530c885a`). A reverting change would reintroduce the disposal-race log-noise fixes that #334568 also landed and would not correct the underlying content-insensitivity, so fix-forward is both safer and more complete. Owners to consult: `@pwang347`

## Validation

Could not run `npm ci`, the build, or the unit test in this environment (dependency install and node execution are blocked by the sandbox). The change is verified by source inspection: `hashBytes` iterates every content byte seeded with the length, so the two 17-byte reference-file variants in the failing test hash differently, making `updatedResult.ref.nonce !== result.ref.nonce` hold. TypeScript usage is consistent (`VSBuffer.buffer` is a `Uint8Array`; `numberHash` is exported from `base/common/hash`).

## Risk

Low and bounded. The change is confined to nonce derivation inside `SyncedCustomizationBundler`. Behavior is strictly more correct: the nonce now changes in more cases (content edits) and is stable across unrelated metadata churn (e.g. `mtime`-only touches no longer force a re-sync). No public API changes.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@pwang347`

**Root cause (upstream publish gap, not a VS Code integration bug):**
The `npm ci` PR check fails with:

pull_requests.title: Carry Chat Editor custom agent through first send
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #335176

## Summary

- carry the mode submitted from an untitled contributed Chat Editor into the real session model created by the first send
- apply the transfer only for the queued or accepted caller after pending-request arbitration, including late sends still addressed to the stale untitled URI
- add regression coverage for stale input state, custom submitted mode, concurrent senders with different modes, and late accepted sends

## Root cause

The Slack repro is a first-send handoff bug, not a custom-agent file/catalog deletion bug:

1. A fresh Chat Editor remembers and displays the real `Data` custom agent.
2. `ChatWidget` submits `hi` with the correct custom `modeInfo`.
3. `ChatService._materializeUntitledSession` creates and loads the real contributed-session model.
4. Materialization carries the untitled model's intended language model, but not its submitted chat mode.
5. The request runs with `Data`, while the real model swapped into the widget still has its default `Agent` mode.

The fix captures the actual submitted mode from `IChatSendRequestOptions.modeInfo` before materialization or stale-resource redirection. It applies that mode to the real model only when that caller is queued or accepted. The untitled input-model mode remains a fallback for programmatic requests that do not provide mode identity.

Applying after arbitration matters: concurrent first sends can materialize one real session but accept a different caller first. The accepted caller—not a rejected materialization owner—must determine the established picker. A later send still addressed to the stale untitled URI similarly transfers its own accepted mode.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- untitled contributed-session materialization suite: **11 passing**
- regression starts with stale `Agent` input state, submits custom `Data` mode information, and verifies the materialized real model stores `Data`
- concurrent regression submits different `Ask` and `Agent` modes and verifies the real model matches whichever request is accepted
- late-send regression submits a different mode through the stale untitled resource and verifies the established model follows the accepted late request
- falsification check: removing the transfer makes the custom-mode regression fail with an undefined real-model mode
- independent code review found no remaining issues
- real Code OSS verification using the VS Code repository's actual `Data` agent:
  - regular Chat Editor;
  - `Copilot` harness;
  - fresh session remembered `Data`;
  - sent `hi`;
  - picker remained `Data` continuously through materialization and active reasoning.

## Manual testing

1. Open the VS Code repository in an editor window.
2. Open **New Chat Editor**.
3. Verify the session harness is **Copilot**.
4. Select the real **Data** custom agent.
5. Send `hi`.
6. While the first request is reasoning and after it completes, verify the picker remains **Data** rather than resetting to **Agent**.
7. Click **New Chat Editor** and repeat the test; every fresh session should preserve Data through its first send.
8. After the first turn, switch between **Agent** and **Data** and send follow-ups to confirm explicit later selections still work.

## Evidence

### Before — exact Slack report and screenshots

https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C0AJZ5319PZ/p1788381749454329

### After — exact first-send flow

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c267bf64-2d91-41fb-a026-37fd3baa54a2

pull_requests.title: nes: fix: encode paths in inline suggestion requests
pull_requests.body:
> **Client-side workaround on hold.** This proposal changes the model-facing path representation. A prompt-preserving service-side cause has now been identified and is being validated instead. Do not merge this encoding change as the preferred root-cause fix.

Fixes #325491.

Related: #334759, #334523, #335001.

## Root cause

NES inserts file paths into unquoted, line-oriented prompt fields and diff-patch headers. Those paths were raw filesystem text. The Windows drive-letter fix in #333429 corrects workspace-relative path selection, but does not make the resulting path safe for the model protocol.

I reproduced the remaining failure on macOS in Code OSS with C# 2.140.9, without Unity Editor or C# Dev Kit. With `copilot-nes-lysithea-24`, the same C# source works under `Weekly-Material/Week-8` and fails under `Weekly Material/Week 8`. Adding a space to a plain C# filename also reproduces it. The separate completions panel still works.

The distinction is present in the incoming SSE choices, before client accumulation or patch parsing:

```text
Before, with the literal spaced path:
{"delta":{"content":""},"finish_reason":"stop"}

After, with an encoded path token:
{"delta":{"content":"Assets/Weekly%20Material/Week%208/Scripts/UnityProbe.cs:11\n"},"finish_reason":null}
```

The encoded request receives the subsequent deletion/addition chunks and produces ghost text. This is not a renderer change or a fallback to classic completions.

## Changes

- Percent-encode path segments in the shared prompt-path formatter. This covers the current file, recent/context files, edit history, and predicted output while preserving path separators and the previous Windows normalization.
- Resolve returned path tokens through one decode-once helper, shared by diff-patch targets and cross-file cursor jumps.
- Preserve literal percent sequences, filename delimiters, Unicode, and notebook-cell fragments. Reject malformed encoding explicitly rather than silently targeting a different file.
- Add regression coverage for serialization consistency, round trips, active-document progressive reveal, cross-file targets, malformed tokens, and cursor-target resolution.

No filesystem paths are renamed, no new setting is introduced, and unified NES remains the suggestions provider.

## Validation

- Focused Vitest suites: **430 passed; 4 Windows-only tests skipped on macOS**.
- Copilot extension TypeScript check passed.
- ESLint passed for all changed files.
- Live Code OSS before/after test, using the same profile and model configuration:
  - Before: spaced paths fail both automatic and explicit triggers; hyphenated control works.
  - After: **12/12 cases show ghost text**: automatic and explicit triggers for nested spaces, a hyphenated control, a filename space, literal `%20` plus a space, `#`/`?` delimiters, and a Unicode filename.
  - Successful items are from the NES provider, not classic completions.

The live test used the dev checkout and miscellaneous C# files in an MIT-licensed Unity sample, not a running Unity 6 project. It establishes the path-sensitive case, not that every related report has the same cause. Native Windows execution remains for CI.


## Before / after

Top: before the fix. Bottom: after the fix, on the same space-containing path. Cropped to the editor; both captures are from real OSS requests.

![Before and after: unified NES suggestions in the same C# file with spaces in its path](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61aa98ef-82c4-4777-a337-959641f78570)

Security fixes

This release includes a fix for the following security issue:

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- serialize Copilot turn event ID reads behind earlier database writes
- prevent chat truncation from racing the persisted SDK event boundary
- add a deterministic regression test for the read-after-write ordering guarantee

## Root cause

The Copilot SDK user-message handler persists its event ID asynchronously. History boundary reads could bypass that pending write, observe the next turn with no event ID, and treat truncation as a no-op. A later model request would then retain conversation context already removed from AHP state.

No replay fixtures or timeouts changed.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files
- SessionDatabase unit suite: 73 passing
- focused Copilot strict replay: 30 consecutive passing runs after the fix
- full Copilot Agent Host E2E replay: 177 passing, 22 expected pending
- complete Agent Host E2E matrix: Conformance, Claude, Codex, and Copilot passed

(Written by Copilot)

The Copilot SDK can emit `session.idle` while the asynchronous `tool.execution_complete` handler is still persisting file-edit metadata. pull_requests.title: fix: resolve win32 product.json path in native policy smoke fixture (build fix for vscode-engineering#3813)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

The "Native Policy Plumbing" smoke tests (Electron, Windows) fail in their `before all` hook with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '...\VSCode-win32-x64\resources\app\product.json'`. Both Policy Plumbing tests throw before any assertion runs, failing the Windows Electron smoke stage on `main`.

## Root cause

`test/smoke/src/areas/policy/nativePolicy.ts` resolved the built product manifest on Windows by joining `resources/app/product.json` onto `path.dirname(getBuildElectronPath(options.codePath))` — effectively the root of the build output. However, the Windows built app nests its payload inside a subdirectory (e.g. `VSCode-win32-x64`). `getBuildElectronPath` itself accounts for this: for win32 it uses the `findFilePath` helper in `test/automation/src/electron.ts`, which searches one level of subdirectories for `resources/app/product.json`. The fixture bypassed that logic and assumed the file lived directly under the root, so `fs.readFileSync` hit a non-existent path and threw.

## How the fix works

Added an exported `getBuildProductPath(root)` helper in `test/automation/src/electron.ts` that resolves `product.json` per-platform, reusing the existing `findFilePath` subdirectory search on win32 (the same mechanism `getBuildElectronPath`/`getBuildVersion` already use). `nativePolicy.ts` now calls `getBuildProductPath(options.codePath)` instead of hand-rolling the path, so the Windows nested layout is handled correctly and darwin/linux behavior is preserved. This corrects the invalid path producer rather than guarding the consumer or swallowing the error.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back.** Public culprit: PR microsoft/vscode#335107 (commit `644fe2ac`), which introduced the fixture. The regression is isolated to new test-fixture path resolution with no product/runtime/schema impact, and this fix-forward is a small, bounded correction that reuses existing, proven path-resolution logic. Reverting would only remove the new smoke coverage. Owners to consult: `@rwoll`

## Validation

Source inspection only. `getBuildElectronPath` (win32) and `getBuildVersion` (win32) already rely on `findFilePath` to locate `resources/app/product.json` within a subdirectory of the build root, confirming the nested layout; the new helper reuses the identical resolution. TypeScript type checking / smoke test execution could not be run in this environment (the `tsc` and build tooling were unavailable to the agent).

## Risk

Low. The change is confined to test automation/smoke code, adds a helper that mirrors existing behavior, and leaves the non-Windows paths functionally unchanged.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@rwoll`

pull_requests.title: agentHost: defer busy CI reruns without blocking repairs
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- Keep Agent Merge repairing newly failed checks while other CI jobs are still running.
- Defer and coalesce busy workflow reruns in the existing controller, without model polling or extra repair turns while waiting.
- Suppress only the recorded failures, so newly failing sibling jobs and new attempts remain actionable.
- Revalidate the pull request head, authorization, and workflow attempt before rerunning; discard stale requests and handle shutdown races.
- Distinguish deferred, requested, and unconfirmed reruns in the tool transcript.

## Why

The retry failure investigated on #335083 occurred after the macOS job failed but before the overall workflow finished. The rerun tool required an aggregate failure conclusion and incorrectly treated the unfinished workflow as unavailable. This fixes the rerun path without making CI repair wait for all checks to finish.

Deferred requests are scoped to the current Agent Host runtime and reuse its existing refresh/backstop loop and GitHub mutation API. No new scheduler or configuration is introduced.

## Validation

- 76 focused tests passed across the Agent Merge rerun, controller, server-tool, gate, and prompt suites.
