pull_requests.title: agentHost: Correlate stalled client tool calls
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- add the existing tool call ID to Agent Host stall and post-stall completion telemetry
- capture the delegated executor client connection state when a client tool stalls
- preserve the bounded connection-state snapshot on the eventual completion event
- cover connected, disconnected, unknown, and non-client blocker cases

## Motivation

Claude client-executed tools frequently remain delegated beyond the five-minute stall threshold. The existing stall and completion events could not be joined, so they could not measure recovery or distinguish a disconnected executor from a connected but nonresponsive one.

This change adds no new events and does not alter tool execution, cancellation, authentication, confirmation, or timeout behavior. It reports no raw client identifier or tool content.

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostToolCallTelemetry.test.ts` (19 passing)

pull_requests.title: Preserve established custom agent selection across catalog gaps
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #308525

## Summary

- keep an established Agent Host session's selected custom agent authoritative while its catalog hydrates
- restrict remembered-agent initialization to untitled sessions that do not already have an explicit selection
- cover first-send graduation, background completion, custom/default A/B switching, repeated close/reopen hydration, and remote Agent Host providers

## Root cause

`AgentHostAgentPickerContribution._initAgent` mixed two responsibilities:

1. seed a remembered agent into a new untitled session;
2. clear an established selection when the current custom-agent catalog did not contain its URI.

The second operation was unsafe. During first-send graduation, background hydration, close/reopen, and remote reconnects, the Agent Host can publish a non-empty but temporarily incomplete catalog. The picker interpreted that snapshot as permanent deletion and called `setAgent(undefined)`, clearing both the session facade and the remembered picker preference.

The fix limits `_initAgent` to its actual initialization role: an unselected untitled session may be seeded from the remembered preference; an established session is never mutated merely because a catalog snapshot does not currently resolve its selected URI. Explicitly choosing default `Agent` still clears the selection through the normal user-action path.

## Original repro coverage

| Reported scenario | Coverage |
| --- | --- |
| Custom agent changes to `Agent` during the first turn | The current provider already carries the picked agent onto the committed session. This PR prevents a partial committed-session catalog from immediately clearing it. Real-agent first-send verification passed. |
| Session completes while the user works in another session | The custom session remains authoritative while inactive. Real-agent background completion passed. |
| Switch between custom session A and default session B | Five real UI cycles passed: A remained custom and B remained `Agent`. The regression test also verifies the default session is never seeded from A. |
| Close and reopen the same session repeatedly | Five real close/reopen cycles passed. The picker model retains the selected ID during a catalog gap and emits a label refresh when the mode returns. |
| Remote Tunnel / SSH Agent Host | The same provider-neutral contribution handles local and `agenthost-*` providers. A remote provider-ID regression and the full remote provider suite pass. |
| Original Worktree video | The repository-to-worktree URI transition was separately fixed by #323548/#323566. Those changes carry the selection through graduation, rebase it to the worktree twin, and hydrate it from the draft. The existing worktree-rebase regression also passes. This PR adds the remaining protection against destructive partial-catalog cleanup. |
| `Mark as Done` / missing Changes panel content | Separate changes-state issue; not changed by this PR. |

The file-removal scenario used earlier is not required to reproduce the user flow. It is only a deterministic stress case for the same state boundary: a selected URI is temporarily absent while the catalog remains non-empty.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Agent Host picker, scoped mode-picker, and full remote provider suites: **92 passing**
- existing worktree custom-agent rebase regression: passing
- regression matrix covers:
  - untitled → committed graduation with a non-empty incomplete catalog;
  - completion while another default-Agent session is active;
  - repeated custom/default A/B switching;
  - three fresh-facade reopen/hydration cycles;
  - remote `agenthost-*` providers;
  - unchanged remembered-agent seeding for untitled sessions;
  - consumer-observed picker fallback and label recovery events.
- falsification check: restoring the pre-fix cleanup branch makes the graduation/reopen test clear the local selection four times and the remote test clear it once; the untitled initialization test still passes
- real Code OSS Agents Window using an authenticated Copilot Agent Host and a real workspace `.agent.md` file:
  - the first turn executed the custom instructions and returned `CUSTOM-308525`;
  - the picker recovered the custom label after graduation;
  - the custom session completed while a default session was active;
  - five A/B cycles preserved custom A and default B independently;
  - five close/reopen cycles restored the custom label and transcript markers.

## Manual testing

1. In a disposable workspace, add a real custom agent such as `.github/agents/persistence.agent.md`:

   ```md
   ---
   name: Persistence Agent
   description: Verifies custom-agent persistence.
   tools: [read]
   ---

   Read `marker.txt` before replying. End every response with exactly `CUSTOM-308525`.
   ```

2. Add `marker.txt`, open the **Agents Window**, select the workspace, choose **Copilot**, and select **Persistence Agent**.
3. Send `Read marker.txt and briefly confirm what it contains.`
4. Verify that after the session graduates and completes:
   - the picker returns to **Persistence Agent** if it briefly shows a hydration fallback;
   - the response ends with `CUSTOM-308525`.
5. Send another marker request, then immediately open a new session and leave it on default **Agent**. Let the custom session complete in the background.
6. Switch between the custom session and default session at least five times. Verify the custom session always shows **Persistence Agent** and the default session always shows **Agent**.
7. On the custom session, choose **More Actions... > Close**, then reopen it from the Sessions list. Repeat at least five times and verify the custom label and marker responses return each time.
8. Optional Worktree variant: use a Git workspace, enable **Worktree**, and repeat the first-send flow. Verify the custom agent remains selected after the workspace changes to the generated worktree.
9. Optional remote variant: repeat through a Tunnel or SSH Agent Host and verify the custom selection survives reconnect/reopen hydration.
10. Explicitly choose default **Agent** on a session and verify it remains default; the fix must not restore a custom agent after an intentional user change.

### Optional deterministic stress case

Temporarily make only the selected `.agent.md` unavailable while another custom agent remains in the catalog, then restore it. The picker may show `Agent` while unavailable, but it must recover the original custom label after discovery catches up.

### After — exact first-send, A/B, and close/reopen flows

pull_requests.title: chat: avoid watching Copilot CLI plugin contents
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334391

## What was happening

Shared plugin discovery watches each plugin root and its manifest and component paths (`commands`, `skills`, `agents`, `hooks`, and so on). These watchers make in-place edits show up immediately, but for Copilot CLI-installed plugins they leave `ReadDirectoryChangesW` handles inside CLI-owned directories. Windows then prevents the CLI from renaming or deleting those directories during an atomic install, update, or uninstall, resulting in `Access is denied`.

## Why content watchers can be skipped here

CLI-installed plugin directories are managed snapshots: the supported update path replaces the whole plugin directory rather than editing its contents in place. CLI discovery already watches the `installed-plugins` ancestors and each marketplace bucket, which is enough to observe those directory swaps. On a bucket change, this fix rebuilds the CLI plugin entry instead of reusing its cached contents, so the replacement still appears without a reload. Hidden transaction directories are ignored, while other plugin discovery sources retain their existing content watchers for live in-place edits.

## Verification

- Reproduced before the fix in a full Code OSS window on Windows: after opening Agent Customizations and confirming the fixture plugin was discovered, renaming its installed plugin root failed with `Access to the path ... is denied`; the same rename succeeded before launch and after closing Code OSS.
- Verified the fix in a freshly rebuilt full Code OSS window: renamed the installed plugin to a hidden sibling, created its replacement at the original path, and deleted the old directory while Code OSS remained open. All operations succeeded, and Agent Customizations automatically changed from `VS Code 334391 Repro` to `VS Code 334391 Replacement` without a reload.
- Added focused coverage for excluding hidden transaction directories, avoiding watchers at or below CLI plugin roots, and rebuilding replacement plugin contents.
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted ESLint for the changed TypeScript files
- `scripts\test.bat --grep "AgentPlugin format detection"` (48 passing)

pull_requests.title: nes: fix: preserve viewport when accepting multi-line edits
pull_requests.body:
cc @hediet

## Summary

Preserve the editor viewport when accepting a multi-line next edit suggestion (NES).

Multi-line NES rendering uses a view zone to reserve space before the suggested lines exist in the model. Acceptance inserts real lines and then removes that redundant zone, so removal must not apply the compensation used for ordinary dismissal.

## Root cause

The acceptance guard in `AdditionalLinesWidget` still checked the legacy edit source `inlineSuggestion.accept`.

Inline completion acceptance now reaches `CodeEditorWidget.onBeforeExecuteEdit` as the typed source `inlineCompletionAccept`. The stale comparison never matched, so acceptance was treated like dismissal and `keepCursorStable` subtracted the removed zone height from `scrollTop`.

For a seven-line suggestion, this moved the viewport upward by exactly seven lines.

## Fix

Recognize `inlineCompletionAccept` when suppressing view-zone removal compensation.

This restores the intended acceptance behavior while retaining compensation for non-accept dismissal.

## Regression coverage

The new browser tests use a real, laid-out `CodeEditorWidget` and the production `InlineEditsInsertionView`:

- accepting a seven-line insertion preserves both `scrollTop` and a stable screen-space anchor;
- dismissing the same insertion after moving the cursor below it still compensates and preserves the cursor's screen-space position.

## Validation

- Targeted Electron browser tests: 3 passing
- ESLint on both changed files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Real Code OSS before/after scenarios: baseline jumps from line 75 to 68; fixed build remains at line 75

## Before / after

**Before — acceptance jumps upward by seven lines**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ba3187d-8870-4ad7-96b7-a5ea9807290c

**After — acceptance preserves the viewport anchor**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07669c72-b821-4ff7-bf65-81bde46a3e07

pull_requests.title: agentHost: switch Auto routing preferences with the SDK
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #333809.

## Summary

- Remove launch-time Auto routing profile pinning, the frozen launch-plan tier, and local SDK CAPI type widening.
- Forward the selected Auto preference through SDK `setModel`, alongside reasoning effort and context size. Send explicit `null` to reset Auto routing preferences; omit the option for concrete models.
- Resolve create-time preferences from the model selection and shared settings, including empty-history resume fallbacks. Ordinary resume preserves runtime-owned routing state; subsequent model changes apply through `setModel`.
- Persist the requested preference rather than rewriting it to the launch profile, and preserve prior metadata when the SDK rejects a change.
- Unify Auto-tier enablement and override settings across Copilot Chat and agent-host sessions, using the shared workbench-owned experiment default.
- Align model-picker labels, hover text, and accessibility help with the Auto "Optimize for" preferences.

pull_requests.title: agentHost: only remove worktree on archive when in sync with remote
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Tightens the safety policy for automatic worktree removal on session archive. Previously `_cleanupWorktreeOnArchive` in `worktreeIsolation.ts` committed any uncommitted changes and then removed the worktree, relying on branch preservation for reversibility. This changes the gate so the worktree is **only removed when git is fully up to date with its remote**:

- the branch tracks an upstream branch,
- there are no unpushed commits (`outgoingChanges === 0`), and
- the working tree is clean (`uncommittedChanges === 0`).

The new `_isBranchUpToDateWithRemote` helper **fails closed** — if the git state can't be determined, the branch has no upstream, or there is any local-only work, the worktree is left intact so nothing is ever discarded. The existing checks (worktree already gone, branch missing) and the reversible unarchive-recreate flow are unchanged.

## Why

Auto-removal should never risk losing local-only work. Requiring the branch to be in sync with the remote is a stronger, easier-to-reason-about guarantee than committing-then-removing, and it matches the intent that removal is a safe, reversible disk-space optimization.

## Testing

- New test: `cleanup on archive keeps the worktree when the branch is not up to date with its remote` — covers no-upstream, unpushed commits, uncommitted changes, and unknown git state.
- Existing `cleanup on archive removes a clean worktree and unarchive recreates it` still passes.
- Full `WorktreeIsolation` suite: 41 passing.
- ESLint clean on changed files.

## Notes for reviewers

This is intentionally independent of the auto-archive/auto-delete settings work in #334341; that PR's only worktree change is the delete-time `canAutomaticallyDeleteArchivedSession` gate and does not touch `_cleanupWorktreeOnArchive`.

pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334868

Agent Host skill completions already opt in through their `/` trigger character, which opens suggestions for the initial slash and keeps refreshing an active completion session. After deleting back to bare `/`, however, typing the next character requires Monaco quick suggestions to start a new session.

`ChatInputPart` intentionally disables quick suggestions by default because it hosts inline prompt completions. The standalone Sessions composer does not override Monaco's inline-aware quick-suggestion default, which is why the comparison surface retriggers correctly.

Add a typed construction option to `ChatInputPart` and enable it only for the Automation dialog with `offWhenInlineCompletions`. Other Chat inputs keep their existing default, while Automations match the Sessions behavior and still give inline prompt completions precedence.

- Actual Code OSS Dev window on macOS arm64 (1.138.0): type `/act`, delete back to `/`, then type `act` again. The original behavior never reopened suggestions; the fix reopened and filtered the skill list.

pull_requests.title: fix: center the fork glyph in the chat checkpoint toolbar
pull_requests.body: Fixes #335071 ### Problem The fork button's glyph sits about 2px left of center, leaving a visible gap along its right edge. | Before | After | |---|---| | | | ### Cause `ChatForkActionViewItem` renders the glyph inside a nested `.chat-fork-action-icon` span. The shared actionbar rule (`actionbar.css`) sizes any descendant codicon to a 16x16 flex box and centers it vertically, but never horizontally. The checkpoint toolbar renders this icon at the **compact 12px** size, so the glyph was left-aligned inside a 16px box and the unused 4px landed on the right. The button's own padding was already symmetric, so the offset came entirely from the inner box. ### Fix One scoped declaration in `chat.css`, added to the fork-label rule that already exists in the checkpoint block: ```css .chat-fork-action-icon { justify-content: center; } ``` Deliberately unchanged: button size, padding, divider lines, separator dot, **Restore Checkpoint** placement, tooltip, focus ring, and the ARIA busy/label handling. No `!important`, no positional offsets, no `:has()`, and no change to the global actionbar styling that other toolbars rely on. Both the chat view and the Agents Window go through the shared `ChatForkActionViewItem`, so no window-specific override is needed. ### Tests Extended `chatForkActionViewItem.test.ts` to render the view item inside a production-shaped checkpoint toolbar hierarchy against the real stylesheet, asserting centered alignment and unchanged button dimensions across **idle -> running -> completed**. The compact loading spinner reuses the same span, so the running state is covered too. The existing spinner and accessibility assertions are preserved. ### Verification - The regression test fails on the pre-fix CSS (`glyphAlignment: 'normal'` in all three states) and passes with the fix - `chatForkActionViewItem` and `chatRestoreCheckpointActionViewItem` suites pass - `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/media/chat.css` passes - Measured the real glyph pseudo-element over CDP in a running build: horizontal offset moved from **-1.999px to -0.003px** in both the chat view and the Agents Window, with button width and height unchanged

pull_requests.title: automations: fix: honor worktree and provider session configuration
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

An automation stores two different kinds of state. Its target identifies the provider, agent/session type, workspace, isolation mode, and base branch. Its provider-owned session template stores model selection and model options, a custom agent, and native configuration such as Mode and Approvals.

Both must survive editing and later execution. The browser can dispatch a legacy automation, while a migrated automation runs directly in the Agent Host, including after a host restart. Saved preferences are not permission grants: the current provider schema and managed policy still determine effective behavior.

## What was broken

The Automation dialog gated New Worktree on a Copilot-CLI-only declaration, even though worktree isolation is implemented by the shared host for other agents, including Claude and Codex. It also asked the local Git extension for every target's repository. That extension rejects remote workspace URIs, so merely enabling the checkbox would not fix remote automations.

Several adjacent configuration paths were also incomplete:

- Generic provider configuration lived in the ordinary composer's repository toolbar, which the Automation dialog did not render.
- Cloud model restoration updated the displayed model but bypassed the extension's model option. A late option catalogue could therefore disagree with the displayed selection.
- Cloud Sandbox routing came from an unrelated ordinary-composer preference rather than the saved automation.
- Restored fallback-CLI approval preferences overwrote the initially policy-clamped value.
- A host automation inherited its creation-time model into the first message, but not its selected custom agent.
- Host-generated session IDs were marked worktree-pending too late to prevent Codex prewarming in the source checkout.
- Codex workspace-agent URI matching did not account for worktree execution, especially when subsequent or restored turns repeated the original agent selection.

## How the fixes work

### Provider-owned worktree discovery

`ISessionsProvider.getWorktreeOptions` now exposes workspace-specific worktree support, the current branch, initial branch choices, and an optional loader for incomplete result sets.

Agent Host providers resolve these choices on the selected host. Branch searches reuse that resolved configuration rather than re-resolving the full schema for every query. Providers without the operation retain the existing local Git path.

This keeps shared Automation UI provider-neutral. The static Agent Host declaration no longer singles out Copilot; the host's workspace schema determines whether worktrees can actually be chosen.

Remote completion windows are not treated as complete branch inventories. A saved or searched branch outside the initial window is not falsely marked unavailable. Search immediately removes selectable stale results, exposes loading, supports cancellation and retry, and resumes correctly after an IME composition is cancelled without changing the query. Related target/provider notifications are coalesced before starting repository work.

If a saved Worktree target becomes unsupported, its checkbox can still be unchecked. The user explicitly opts into Folder execution; the dialog does not silently weaken isolation.

### Provider-native session controls and preferences

The Automation controls reuse native provider configuration pickers. Generic enum/boolean settings are available alongside dedicated provider Mode and Approvals controls, without duplicating worktree/branch controls or exposing transient/session-only fields.

Cloud automations can display and save the existing Sandbox choice. Restoration does not rewrite ordinary-composer defaults. Explicit picker changes retain the existing shared-default semantics.

Cloud model selection now synchronizes its extension option through the same path for interactive changes, template restoration, and late option discovery. Canonical values take precedence over compatibility aliases, and unknown provider preferences remain intact.

Fallback CLI approvals retain the saved preference separately from the policy-effective observable value. Display and execution use the effective value; capture preserves unchanged intent.

### Execution and custom agents

The first host automation message inherits creation-time model and agent selections independently, while preserving explicit message overrides.

Session IDs are allocated before provider creation, so both supplied and generated IDs are worktree-pending before eager provider work can start. Failure paths clear the pending state.

Codex resolves original workspace-agent selections at customization launch using host worktree metadata and canonical repository roots. It preserves the original persisted selection rather than rewriting protocol identity. Regression coverage includes repeated `changeAgent` calls, provider reload, linked source checkouts, and plugin/external selections that must not be redirected.

## Provider coverage and intentional limits

| Provider | Worktree behavior | Configuration coverage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local/remote Agent Host Copilot CLI | Host schema and host branch discovery | Model/options, custom agent, native Mode/Approvals, opaque template values |
| Local/remote Agent Host Claude | Same host-owned isolation path | Model/options, custom agent, native permission-mode configuration |
| Local/remote Agent Host Codex | Same path, with pending-start and agent-restoration repairs | Model/options, custom agent, native mode/approval presets |
| Other schema-driven Agent Hosts | Capability comes from the workspace schema, not the provider name | Generic supported controls remain provider-owned |
| Fallback Copilot CLI | Existing local Git/worktree path | Model/options, custom modes/agents, saved versus effective approvals |
| Copilot Cloud | Worktrees remain unsupported | Cloud model option and saved Sandbox routing |

Cloud custom agents and workspace-less Cloud sessions remain unsupported. Transient local Dev Container handoff controls are not newly made into Automation template fields; selecting an existing remote/container host continues through the remote-provider boundary. No new protocol fields, user settings, dependencies, or policy channels are introduced.

## Validation

- **1,195 unit tests passed**, with **27 existing pending tests**, across the affected Automation, provider, Codex, and shared ActionWidget suites.
- **Five strict replay E2E scenarios passed** using the real bundled runtimes and AHP:
  - Host session configuration resolves and completes Git branches.
  - Correct working-directory creation for Copilot CLI, Claude, and Codex.
  - Copilot automation Mode and Approvals survive a host restart and run.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` passed.
- Changed-file ESLint and `git diff --check` passed.

The replay scenarios use committed model traffic, not live model services. Cloud and arbitrary remote deployment behavior is covered at the provider-adapter boundary; no paid Cloud runs or live third-party remote-host jobs were launched.

## Review

Two complete independent four-lens Astra reviews covered architecture, performance, UI/UX, and correctness/simplicity. All findings were addressed with regressions. Astra then independently verified the final IME-cancellation and duplicate-lookup follow-ups and reported no remaining evidence-backed issues in those repairs.

pull_requests.title: Open full output from chat terminal cards
pull_requests.body:
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329724
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/328596

Depends on: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/440

- Preserve the SDK's `shell_exit.outputFilePath` as terminal-associated `fullOutput` metadata through live completion, replay, and chat serialization. No SDK bump is needed.
- Keep the bounded structured preview and append a plain terminal message explaining that output was truncated and where the complete output was saved. Results without a structured reference retain the existing completion-text fallback.
- Add the same icon-only `openInProduct` action used by local terminal cards to the nested executed-command block. For Agent Host output it opens a read-only editor instead of focusing a terminal.
- Route both the displayed saved path and the command-block action to the same canonical read-only virtual resource. The path's higher-priority link provider has no idle underline and cannot fall through to the raw randomized spill file.
- Give each virtual output a short, stable, command-derived name such as `npm-test-7ph3d.txt`, with a five-character suffix to distinguish repeated invocations. Sanitize unsafe names and cap them at 64 characters.
- Fix snapshot reflow so later appends cannot overwrite text at a stale cursor column, and hide the input cursor in read-only terminal snapshots.
- Keep live terminal input, selection, scrolling, local terminal **Show** behavior, and the Terminal Output Accessible View intact.

The protocol sync is pinned to `35af62fb5e06883d8f67d6c6f8640ef81d9fbc16`. It also carries existing upstream authentication-expiry declarations; generated protocol files were not edited by hand.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- File-scoped ESLint for all directly changed TypeScript files
- Stylelint for `chatTerminalToolProgressPart.css`
- 421 targeted unit/browser tests covering:
  - SDK/AHP mapping, serialization, restored history, and old-result fallback
  - canonical URI identity, command-derived names, duplicate outputs, sanitization, lazy reads, retries, and read-only behavior
  - exact path-range interception across wrapped terminal rows, with no idle underline
  - icon and path activation opening the same virtual resource
  - local terminal **Show** behavior, keyboard activation, accessibility help/view, snapshot cursor hiding, and resize/append correctness
- Strict Copilot replay:

  ```sh
  ./scripts/test-integration.sh \
    --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts \
    --grep 'shell full output'
  ```

  The scenario verifies complete 256KB output, retained reference identity after resubscription, and `NotFound` after removing its own test artifact.
- 19 real-parent component fixture variants rendered successfully across expanded, collapsed, empty-preview, no-reference, narrow, long-output, light, dark, and high-contrast states.

### Manual checks

1. Run a command that produces oversized output. Verify the nested executed-command block shows a plain truncation/saved-path message and the same square open icon as a local terminal card.
2. Click the icon, close the editor, then click the displayed saved path. Both should reveal the same short-named, read-only editor—not the raw randomized spill file.
3. Run the large-output prompt twice. Verify the two editors have readable, distinct names and reopen their own content.
4. Resize the chat while the preview is visible. Verify the preview does not show an input cursor and later output cannot overwrite text in the middle.
5. Use the icon with keyboard navigation and repeat from Terminal Output Accessible View.

Packaged Windows/Linux/macOS validation and manual VoiceOver/NVDA verification remain merge-readiness checks. Keep this draft dependent on the AHP PR and re-sync its merged revision before declaring the VS Code PR ready.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

pull_requests.title: Fix customization migration hint shown on every request in 'once' mode
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334578

## Problem

`"chat.customizations.migrationHint": "once"` shows the hint on **every** request instead of once per chat session.

Reproduced in a dev build: with `once` set, both turns of a two-message chat showed the hint.

## Cause

`ChatServiceImpl` records that the hint was shown by writing a key into the input model's `contrib` bag:

```ts
model.inputModel.setState({
    contrib: { ...model.inputModel.state.get()?.contrib, [customizationMigrationHintShownStateKey]: true }
});
```

But `ChatInputPart.getCurrentInputState()` rebuilds that bag from scratch and lets only *widget contributions* populate it:

```ts
contrib: {},
...
for (const contrib of this._widget?.contribs || Iterable.empty()) {
    contrib.getInputState?.(state.contrib);
}
```

`_syncInputStateToModel()` passes that state to `InputModel.setState`, which spread `...state` over `...current` — so `contrib` was **replaced** wholesale.

The next input sync after the hint (clearing the input on send, typing, a model or permission change) therefore published a `contrib` without the flag, wiping it. On the following request `hintAlreadyShown` was `false` again, so `once` behaved exactly like `always`.

## Fix

`setState` takes a `Partial<IChatModelInputState>`. Omitted top-level fields are already preserved via `...current`; nested `contrib` should behave the same way rather than being silently dropped one level down. Merge it by key so each writer owns its own keys:

```ts
contrib: { ...current?.contrib, ...state.contrib },
```

This fixes it for every `setState` caller rather than only `ChatInputPart`, and keeps "once per chat session" surviving reloads since `contrib` is already serialized by `toJSON`.

## Validation

- New unit test `inputModel.setState preserves contrib keys owned by other writers`, verified to fail without the fix.
- `chatModel.test.ts` + `chatService.test.ts`: **198 passing**. `typecheck-client` clean.
- Verified live in a dev build with `once`: turn 1 shows the hint, turn 2 does not. Instrumented runtime state confirmed the flag now survives the widget sync, with the widget's own `chatDynamicVariableModel` key merged in alongside it.

## Note on why this escaped tests

The existing `once customization migration hint remains shown after the session is reloaded` test exercises `ChatService` only and never instantiates `ChatInputPart`, so nothing clobbered `contrib`. The new test covers the merge contract at the model layer, which is where any future non-widget writer is protected.

pull_requests.body: Fixes #316940. getWorktreesRoot() now nests worktrees under .git/vscode-worktrees when the repository root is the user's home directory, instead of trying to write to its parent directory (e.g. /home). pull_requests.title: fix: separate PosixShellType.Sh case with POSIX-safe single-quote escaping
pull_requests.body:
#### What does this implement/fix?

POSIX `sh` does not support ANSI-C `$'...'` quoting. The existing code grouped `PosixShellType.Sh` with `Bash` in a fall-through case, so a path containing a single quote produced `$'...\\'...'` — valid in Bash but a syntax error in `/bin/sh`.

**Fix:** Give `PosixShellType.Sh` its own case using the POSIX-portable close-quote/escaped-quote/reopen-quote idiom: replace each `'` with `'\'')`.

Also tightens `collapseTildePath` to check `startsWith(normalizedUserHome + '/')` (or equality) instead of `includes`, so `/home/user2` is not incorrectly collapsed when home is `/home/user`.

Regression tests added for both fixes.

#### AI usage disclosure

I used AI assistance for:
- Research and understanding

pull_requests.title: Fix subagent activity, opening, and completion state
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fix subagent pills losing their connection to the child chat: tool activity remains stuck at "Working on it...", completed background agents still look busy, and opening a subagent can either do nothing or produce an empty editable chat. Also defer each subagent's list entry until its child actually starts, append it in start order without reserving an earlier position, and use friendly names in background-completion notices.

The pill and the "Background agent ... is complete" notification represent the same delegated agent. The notification was arriving through the parent chat while the pill's child-chat subscription had already failed. This is a client-side lifecycle and presentation problem, not evidence that the agent had stopped doing work.

## Findings from the debug exports

Two locally inspected debug bundles covered the missing-activity, blank-editor, and stale-completion cases. Raw logs, transcripts, machine paths, and session identifiers are intentionally not attached.

### Delayed startup strands the parent pill

The reviewer session showed the following sequence on September 7, 2026 (times below are UTC):

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 21:29:26 | Five background `task` calls returned their launch acknowledgments; the parent began subscribing to their prospective child-chat URIs. |
| 21:29:41 | All five subscriptions failed with `AHP_NOT_FOUND` after the 15-second pre-spawn wait. |
| 21:30:07 | The actual subagent chats were registered, approximately 41 seconds after launch. |
| 21:40:41 | One reviewer emitted SDK completion after 142 tool calls; its child chat received `chat/turnComplete` immediately afterward. |
| 21:40:42 | The parent received the separate background-completion notification, but its pill remained visually busy. |

Four reviewers completed in the captured interval; the fifth was still active. Opening a child could establish a fresh, working subscription, explaining why its transcript contained real tool calls while the parent pill remained stale.

There were two holes in recovery:

1. A failed subscription stores an `Error` value asynchronously. `_observeSubagentSession` only had a synchronous `try/catch`, so it left the failed observation registered and the pill marked active.
2. Background launch tools can complete before their children start. The protocol ignores `ChatToolCallContentChanged` for completed tools, so the later discovery block cannot wake a tool-only observer. The session's chat catalog does publish the real child, but the observer was not using that catalog for discovery.

### Startup placeholders and insertion order

Publishing the parent `task` invocation as soon as the launch tool appears reserves an early position in the response, even if the child will not start for some time. Hiding the launch acknowledgment or disabling its open action does not solve that ordering problem: when the same invocation later gains a child, its rich UI expands at the old position, ahead of tools that have already rendered.

The definitive behavior is now **no subagent entry before an actual child turn exists**, followed by append-at-start publication. A prospective URI, successful launch acknowledgment, or available-but-empty child chat does not prove that a subagent has started. Required confirmation/authentication UI remains visible so initialization cannot hide a request that needs user input.

### Completion labels used the routing ID

The SDK's `agent_idle` and `agent_completed` notification metadata already contains a `displayName` and optional task `description`. The shared notification formatter ignored those fields and interpolated `agentId`, producing the unexplained UUIDs in the UI. Both the live listener and restored-history mapper use that formatter, so the fix covers both without a new registry or SDK change. IDs remain unchanged for task routing.

### Other presentation and restore gaps

- **Restored parent state was disconnected.** A completed launch tool in an active-turn snapshot was rendered as a serialized part, while child observation updated a separate, unrendered live invocation.
- **The latest tool was missing or incorrectly worded.** The subagent activity renderer skipped serialized child tools and always used the invocation message rather than the completed tool's past-tense message.
- **Unavailable actions looked clickable.** For a child that has started, losing navigation readiness must disable its open action without replacing its rich presentation or activity.
- **A prospective URI was treated as an openable chat.** The rich editor action could become enabled before the provider had resolved a child chat.
- **Missing chats became blank editable editors.** The load path awaited child subscription hydration without checking its `Error` value. Not-found suppression was also broad enough to hide missing-child failures, and missing child state could fall back to editable interactivity.

## Relevant history

This is a combination of lifecycle assumptions rather than a single rendering-only change:

| Change | Relationship to the failure |
| --- | --- |
| #326169 (`9603ef1ea5f`) | Introduced the bounded 15-second wait for a prospective subagent chat. The client did not recover when that wait expired before a slow/background child was published. |
| #328651 (`d5dd3ab6966`) | Shared the rich subagent presentation with editor chats and enabled opening based on a prospective URI. |
| #331045 (`dcfc4269938`) | Avoided duplicate restored task cards, but left the rendered serialized parent separate from the live invocation receiving child state. |
| #332456 (`908ab0dc0b8`) | Suppressed not-found load errors generally, including missing child chats rather than only root sessions that the host might not know yet. |

## Fixes

### Recover and track the actual child chat

- Await child subscription hydration and route `Error` values through the existing logging and observation cleanup.
- Observe subagent resource membership in the session chat catalog, including discovery after the launch tool has completed.
- Prefer the catalog's child URI and replace an observation when the real resource differs from the provisional one.
- Project only resource/launch-tool identity with equality checking so unrelated catalog status updates do not repeatedly drive discovery.
- Preserve the existing bounded timeout; no timeout increase or polling loop is introduced.

### Keep opening and completion tied to real state

- Add optional `isChatAvailable` metadata for provider-resolved availability, separately from the prospective resource URI.
- Preserve availability through tool updates and history hydration; enable the open action only once the provider has resolved the child chat.
- Restore observable parent invocations for completed subagent launch tools in active turns so the visible pill receives child activity and completion without creating a duplicate card or splitting streamed markdown.
- Once a child has started, keep its rich presentation pill-only, including when the launch tool is complete. Inline results remain available when rich rendering is disabled.
- Keep an already-started child's rich header and activity visible if navigation becomes unavailable. Explain unavailability in the hover instead of showing a clickable cursor.

### Publish new entries only at actual startup

- Track optional `hasStarted` metadata separately from activity and chat availability; legacy invocations without this field retain their existing publication behavior.
- Use a per-response progress publisher to retain unstarted live invocations outside the response list. No placeholder, output disclosure, or empty space is inserted.
- Publish once at the current end of the stream when a child reports an active or historical turn. If the second launch starts first, it appears first, after any intervening normal tool.
- Preserve synchronous setup for hydrated children, completed same-client snapshot adoption, nested tool grouping, and restored markdown ordering.
- Keep original snapshot invocation handles observable while omitting their unstarted UI entries; delayed reconnect discovery can then append them after newer progress.
- Omit still-unstarted entries from enriched history while retaining their observable invocations. Subagent observers belong to the chat session (or root subagent), not the parent turn, so late startup remains observable after parent completion.
- Append late child progress to the original response by request ID without reopening it or sending it to a newer request. Session disposal still releases the child subscriptions.

### Name background-completion notices

- Prefer the SDK `displayName`, then task `description`, then agent type, trimming empty/whitespace-only values.
- Render the resolved name as inline code so it is visually distinct from the completion sentence, for example: Background agent `Renderer reviewer` is complete. Reuse the existing inline-code escaping helper so backticks or markdown in a title remain literal.
- Use a generic background-agent completion/failure message if all display metadata is empty; never fall back to an unexplained UUID.
- Apply the same formatting to idle, completed, and failed agent notices, both live and restored.
- Preserve notification identity, routing, turn creation, and all non-agent notification behavior.

### Show accurate activity and load failures

- Include serialized child tools in activity presentation and prefer completed past-tense messages such as "Searched...".
- Check child subscription errors before constructing history or synthesizing a draft.
- Restrict not-found suppression to root sessions and show a normal load error for missing child chats.
- Keep unresolved subagent editors read-only rather than falling back to an editable empty chat.

### Break thinking at completion notices

A completion notice was being appended without closing the preceding thinking group. Later reasoning and tools could therefore attach to the still-active group above the notice. Independently, the Copilot event mapper reused the parent's pre-notification reasoning part ID, allowing subsequent reasoning deltas to update the earlier protocol part.

- Finalize the current thinking group when rendering a system notification, using the same mode-aware finalization as other thinking boundaries.
- Mount newly created thinking groups when collapsed mode separates a later tool from reasoning. The existing grouped-content fast path assumed the result was already attached; a stricter connected-DOM regression exposed otherwise correctly ordered tool groups that were never mounted.
- Reset the parent reasoning part ID before publishing the notification so subsequent reasoning allocates a new part after it.
- Keep the parent turn and other subagents running; child reasoning streams are not reset.
- Preserve the boundary across repeated notices, streaming updates, completed responses, fresh renderer templates, and restored history. Read-only chats retain their collapsed-preview override.

No SDK dependency bump, generated protocol change, new setting, or telemetry change is included.

### Review follow-up

Commit `6385cc2dc4e` addresses the three PR review threads and the two findings from the additional three-agent review:

- Scope both live and historical child discovery to `(origin.chat, origin.toolCallId)` so reused tool IDs cannot redirect a pill to a sibling's child.
- Preserve subagent metadata and observe child state for other-client launches.
- Reuse completed same-client snapshots rather than emitting duplicate parent invocations.
- Restore nested subagent resources and availability from the correctly scoped catalog entries.
- Do not use success-worded past-tense labels for denied or skipped tools.
- Keep resolved availability on the child observation so local tool preparation cannot overwrite it, and preserve synchronous setup when child state is already hydrated so nested client tools retain their grouping.

Commit `84ac2d966af` corrected a follow-up regression where the availability guard hid the entire rich pill and a completed background launch fell back to the legacy text header. The final append-on-start change supersedes its pre-start behavior: presentation stays rich after startup, but no entry is published before startup.

Commit `39f27153685` handles child subscription errors throughout the observation lifetime, not only during initial hydration. A later error clears availability and activity, freezes timing, releases the failed observer, and permits catalog-driven recovery. The metadata contract now explicitly distinguishes prospective resources from readiness and documents legacy behavior when availability is undefined.

Commit `1d180d2011a` removed the temporary "Subagent output" disclosure that appeared after launch completion but before child startup. Hiding that disclosure was not sufficient to satisfy the clarified no-placeholder requirement; the final progress-publication change also removes the premature pill and its reserved list position.

### Read-only thinking presentation

Commit `531683b7948` makes read-only chats, including subagent chats, always use `collapsedPreview` thinking regardless of the configured style. The override applies consistently to rendering, grouping, and completion in editor and Agents-window chats without modifying user configuration. Cached content is rebuilt when a chat becomes read-only or editable so the displayed style updates immediately. The settings description and accessibility help explain the behavior.

### Component fixture CI follow-up

The CI virtual-time runner exposed four fixture failures that the earlier interactive browser checks did not catch. The full-response fixture called `renderElement` repeatedly without the list's matching `disposeElement` lifecycle, accumulating progressive-render intervals and exhausting the 200-task virtual-time budget.

The fixture now disposes the previous element render before reusing its response template, matching the production list lifecycle. This is a fixture-only correction: no production behavior changes, disabled checks, increased task limits, or screenshot-baseline acceptance.

### Four-model review corrections

The additional Grok 4.6, Sol Fast, GPT-6 Astra and Opus 5 review found three remaining regressions, addressed by commit `2be1758bd75`:

1. **Delayed startup after parent completion:** retain launch metadata, the deferred publisher, and catalog/child observation with the owning session. The original response receives the late entry and child tools while remaining complete, even if a newer request exists. Empty or initially unavailable restored children receive the same recovery path instead of losing their entry permanently.
2. **Failed launch with an existing catalog child:** scoped catalog membership is sufficient to adopt an observable invocation during active-turn restoration, regardless of launch success or a missing embedded child-content block.
3. **Deferred edit markdown escaping collapsed thinking:** the detached-node mount path now accepts only newly created thinking-group roots. An intentionally lazy markdown child remains unmounted until its owning group is expanded.

The late-start path also keeps a provider-observed active child visually active after the parent finishes; parent finalization must not overwrite the child's authoritative lifecycle. Legacy invocations retain the existing force-finalization behavior.

## Validation

- **865 related unit tests passed** for the four-model review fixes, with one pre-existing skipped test. New regressions cover parent completion before child startup, late catalog retry, server/same-client/other-client sources, original-response routing despite a newer request, child completion and session disposal, idle-history startup, failed active-turn restoration, and lazy edit containment/expansion.
- **16/16 component fixtures passed** using the CI-style renderer and virtual-time checks, including new dark/light fixtures where both subagents start after the parent response is already complete.
- **14/14 subagent fixtures passed twice** with the same component-explorer CLI and virtual-time/error checks used by CI. All repeat screenshot hashes match, and the ten previously passing fixture screenshots are unchanged. The pre-fix run reproduced all four CI failures.
- **767 targeted unit tests passed** for the startup-order follow-up, with **one pre-existing skipped test**. This covers lifecycle, server/same-client/other-client publication and reconnect ordering, state conversion, rich rendering, and live/restored completion notices.
- Earlier read-only validation passed **285 related tests**, with one pre-existing skipped test. Seven new cases cover every configured style, read-only transitions, grouping/completion, settings preservation, and accessibility help.

pull_requests.title: sessions: back the checkpoint and fork rows over a chat background
pull_requests.body:
The **Restore Checkpoint**, **Start Over** and fork controls in the conversation are transparent at rest — only `:hover` gives them a fill (`chat.css:4379`, `chat.css:4410`). Neither row sits inside the opaque `.request-hover`; all three are siblings on `rowContainer` (`chatListRenderer.ts:1084/1100/1172`). So over a chat background they read straight on the wallpaper.

This is the same gap #334655 closed for the new-session composer, one level up in the transcript.

### What changed

One rule in the sessions layer, scoped to `.has-chat-background`. It backs **the toolbar and its sibling text with one opaque plate** rather than plating each control — the move `chat.css:4574-4580` already makes for the editor-instance restore row.

Plating the container instead of the controls buys three things:

- The controls stay transparent, so their existing hover fill composites over the plate. No specificity fight with `chat.css:4410`.
- The `.confirming` Restore Checkpoint pill still owns its own surface and keeps its `background-clip: text` gradient (`chat.css:4422-4437`). No exception needed.
- No permanent border where today only hover draws one. The rows keep their quiet divider tier.

`.checkpoint-dot-separator` is the one selector beyond the editor-instance precedent: it sits between the label and the toolbar on the restore row, so leaving it out would strand it on the wallpaper between two plates.

Appearance without a chat background is untouched — nothing in workbench `chat.css` changes.

### Verification

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "Sessions - Chat View"` — 31 passing. The new case builds both rows under a backed and a plain `.part.sessionspart` and snapshots the four fills against `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`.
- Checked live in an Agents window over the codicon wallpaper. `.checkpoint-container .monaco-toolbar` computes `rgb(25, 26, 27)` (`--session-view-background`); "Restore Checkpoint · ⑂" reads as one continuous band, and the hover fill still lands on top.
- `.checkpoint-restore-container` has `gap: 4px`, so its three plates leave two 4px seams. They're invisible in practice — the row reads as one band. If a busier image ever exposes them, the fix is a `box-shadow` bleed on the plated elements, which closes the gaps without touching layout. Not adding it preemptively.

pull_requests.title: automations: feat: backport AHP lifecycle telemetry to 1.137
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Backport the AHP-owned Automation telemetry from #334981 to `release/1.137`, including native run identifiers.

Browser-owned feature events missed normal Agent Host operations. This gives definition changes and admitted runs one authoritative event family, with the identifiers needed to join existing session and usage telemetry.

## Event contract

| Event | Recorded after |
|---|---|
| `automation.created` | A new non-imported definition is persisted |
| `automation.updated` | Editable definition changes are persisted |
| `automation.deleted` | An existing definition is removed |
| `automation.runCreated` | A manual or scheduled run claim is durably persisted |
| `automation.runStarted` | A non-terminal run receives its first durable primary-session link |
| `automation.runCompleted` | The first persisted terminal transition |

Separating admission from session linkage keeps failures before session creation in the run denominator:

```text
Normal execution:    runCreated -> runStarted -> runCompleted
Pre-session failure: runCreated -------------> runCompleted
```

Completion distinguishes success, error, cancellation, timeout, and restart interruption. Explicit cause tracking avoids classifying localized error text, and completion/cancellation races retain the actual terminal result.

## Configuration and existing telemetry

- Definition and claim/start events include bounded saved configuration: provider, model selection, mode, approvals, isolation, target kind, folder count, and custom-agent presence.
- Complete stored definition resource URIs stay hashed because clients can supply them; authority, query, and fragment distinctions are preserved. Host-generated run UUIDs and linked session IDs stay native.
- Definition/claim events preserve omitted provider selections as `default`; linked-session events report the actual provider.
- Updates explicitly flag title-only edits with `titleChanged`, without collecting the title.
- `(provider, agentSessionId)` joins the run to existing Agent Host turn/token/credit events. This is not a second billing pipeline.
- Typed GDPR metadata covers all six events, including the native run-ID description. Existing usage-telemetry controls still apply.
- No prompts, titles, paths, branches, agent URIs, arbitrary configuration, or raw errors are added to Automation events.

## Release scope and risk

- Same production telemetry implementation as the main PR; no unrelated main-only feature changes.
- Retire the overlapping browser create/update/delete/run/runError/migration events. Keep fallback execution and migration diagnostic logs.
- No protocol, persisted status, scheduler policy, GA setting, or permission-policy changes.
- Preserve the release branch's test scaffolding; do not pull in unrelated main-only regression tests.

The stream intentionally replaces the old feature events rather than dual-writing them. Telemetry remains best-effort, device activity is not person-level engagement, and token/credit completeness remains dependent on provider reporting. No historical backfill is included.

## Validation

- 254 focused Automation tests passed on `release/1.137`, covering the host lifecycle, browser store/runner/scheduler/tools, provider routing, and host projection.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Targeted ESLint and whitespace checks passed.
- The host telemetry implementation and host regression tests match the main PR.
- All six GDPR schemas and native-ID example payloads were validated in the main implementation.
- The shared Copilot review fixes passed 42 host tests on both targets, preserving default provider selections and complete definition resource identities.

CI on this PR validates the release target independently.

pull_requests.title: automations: feat: unify AHP lifecycle telemetry
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Make the authoritative Agent Host the single producer of Automation lifecycle telemetry, with definition/run/session correlation for adoption, execution health, and usage analysis.

Release/1.137 counterpart: #334984.

The previous browser-owned events missed normal AHP-owned operations. Generic Agent Host turn events could identify Automation-origin messages, but did not provide a definition/run identity or count attempts that failed before a session existed. Keeping two feature event families would also leave ambiguity about which source to count.

## Event contract

| Event | Recorded after |
|---|---|
| `automation.created` | A new definition is persisted; replay and imported definitions are excluded |
| `automation.updated` | Editable values change and are persisted; no-op and migration bookkeeping are excluded |
| `automation.deleted` | An existing definition is removed; repeated removals are excluded |
| `automation.runCreated` | A new manual or scheduled run claim is durably persisted |
| `automation.runStarted` | The first primary-session link of a non-terminal run is persisted |
| `automation.runCompleted` | The first non-terminal-to-terminal transition is persisted |

`runCreated` and `runStarted` deliberately measure different milestones. Session creation can fail, so admission must be counted before a session exists:

```text
Normal execution:    runCreated -> runStarted -> runCompleted
Pre-session failure: runCreated -------------> runCompleted
```

Completion distinguishes `success`, `error`, `cancelled`, `timeout`, and `interrupted`. Cancellation cause is tracked explicitly rather than inferred from error text; a successful completion that wins a cancellation race remains successful. Restart recovery records interruption when it observes a persisted running run.

## Configuration and joins

- Definition events and both claim/start events include bounded saved configuration: provider, model selection, mode, approvals, isolation, workspace/quick-chat target, folder count, and custom-agent presence.
- `automationId` hashes the complete stored resource URI because definition identities can be client-supplied; authorities, queries, and fragments remain distinguishable.
- Definition/claim events preserve omitted provider selections as `default`; linked-session events report the actual provider.
- `runId` is the native host-generated run UUID. `agentSessionId` remains native and, with `provider`, matches existing Agent Host session/turn telemetry.
- Trusted catalogue model IDs use the existing model-sanitization helper; BYOK and unknown models are categorized.
- Updates report Boolean change flags, including `titleChanged` for title-only edits, not the changed title, prompt, or configuration contents.

The three run events form one run-level record. Its session can be joined to existing `agentHost.turnCompleted` token/credit fields and diagnostic events; this PR does not duplicate billing counters or modify the existing turn-event payloads.

## Scope and compatibility

- Retire browser `automation.create`, `automation.update`, `automation.delete`, `automation.run`, `automation.runError`, and `automation.migration` emitters. Migration diagnostic logs and fallback execution behavior remain.
- Keep scheduling, persistence, protocol statuses, feature flags, and permission policies unchanged.
- All six events use typed GDPR classifications, field comments, owner metadata, and existing usage-telemetry controls. No prompts, titles, paths, branches, custom-agent URIs, arbitrary configuration, or raw error messages are added.
- Persistence precedes emission, but delivery is best-effort, not exactly-once. Missing completion remains unobserved rather than an inferred outcome.
- Configuration describes saved preferences, not guessed runtime defaults. Token/credit reporting remains provider-dependent; device activity is not person-level engagement.

This intentionally replaces the old feature stream rather than dual-writing it. Historical data is not backfilled.

## Implementation

- Add the six typed publishers in `agentHostAutomationTelemetry.ts` and emit at authoritative commit points in `AgentHostAutomationService`.
- Reuse the existing Agent Host model-sanitization helper.
- Remove browser telemetry dependencies and telemetry-only bookkeeping.
- Extend host tests for persistence failures, replay, imports, pre-session failure, claim/linkage/completion correlation, configuration snapshots, cancellation races, timeout, restart recovery, and joins to existing message telemetry.

## Validation

- 261 focused Automation tests passed across the host service, browser store/runner/scheduler/tools, provider routing, and Agent Host projection.
- Client typechecking passed on the final PR tree.
- Targeted ESLint and whitespace checks passed.
- The existing telemetry extractor resolved all six GDPR schemas, including the native run-ID description.
- Synthetic event examples matched the actual publishers.
- Follow-up Copilot review fixes passed 42 host tests, targeted ESLint, and all six GDPR schema checks.

This is instrumentation validation, not a claim of production ingestion or uniform provider usage coverage.

pull_requests.title: Await session state before computing the customization migration hint
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334953
Fixes #334553

## Problem

The customization migration hint is missing on the **first** request of a new chat, for every Agent Host harness (verified with Copilot, Claude and Codex). Sending a second message in the same chat immediately shows the correct hint, and the Customizations overview shows the correct counts even before any request.

## Cause

Both the hint and the overview use the same `ICustomizationMigrationService.computeMigration(...)`, so this is not a difference in candidate discovery — it is a race on *when* the shared computation reads session state.

`provideSourceFolders()` resolves migration destinations from `IAgentHostCustomizationService.getCustomizations()`, which reads an AHP subscription synchronously:

```ts
customizations: sessionState?.customizations ?? [],
```

`IAgentSubscription.value` is documented as `undefined` until the first snapshot arrives, and `_ensureSessionStateSubscription` creates the subscription on demand — so the first read after creation always yields `undefined`, which the `?? []` collapses into "no customizations".

Subscriptions are keyed by the **chat UI resource**. On first send, `_materializeUntitledSession()` swaps the untitled resource (`agent-host-PROVIDER:/untitled-<uuid>`) for a freshly minted real resource. The hint then runs against that brand-new resource, so a subscription is created at that instant, has no snapshot, and every migration candidate is filtered out — silently, indistinguishable from "nothing to migrate".

Anything reading later (the reactive overview, the second request) sees the arrived snapshot, which is why only the first request is affected. It also explains why the symptom looks intermittent: when the subscription happens to be warm, the hint appears.

## Fix

Add `whenCustomizationsReady(sessionResource, token)` to `IAgentHostCustomizationService` and await it in `provideSourceFolders()`, so one-shot callers can distinguish "not loaded yet" from "no customizations".

- `WorkbenchAgentHostCustomizationService` waits for the subscription's first snapshot (an `Error` also counts as settled).
- The base and null implementations resolve immediately; their targets are backed by already-materialized provider state.
- `getCustomizations()` stays synchronous — reactive UI should keep reading the current value and re-rendering on `onDidChangeCustomizations`.

The wait is **bounded (2s) and cancellable**: the chat request path awaits the hint in a blocking `Promise.all` before sending the user's message, so an unbounded wait would risk delaying the first message. On timeout the caller falls back to today's behaviour.

This mirrors the existing readiness pattern in this area — `computeMcpServerMigration()` already does `await scope.whenResolved()` for the MCP half of the same service.

## Validation

- New unit tests cover the deferred-then-resolved path, the already-loaded path, and the subscription-failure path.
- `agentHostCustomizationService.test.ts`, `customizationMigrationServiceImpl.test.ts`, `remoteAgentHostCustomizationHarness.test.ts`: **26 passing**.
- `npm run typecheck-client` clean.
- Verified live in a dev build: a fresh Copilot chat now shows `Found 1 user customization file that is present but not used by Copilot and could be migrated.` on the **first** message.

Note: #334938 / #334942 is a separate Claude-specific gap (missing destinations on *every* request). That fix is still needed; this one addresses the first-request timing for all harnesses.

* fix: await session state before computing migration hint

The customization migration hint reads migration destinations through
AgentCustomizationItemProvider.provideSourceFolders, which resolves them
from a session-state subscription. IAgentSubscription.value is undefined
until its first snapshot arrives, and the workbench service collapses
that to an empty customization list.

Session-state subscriptions are keyed by chat UI resource. On the first
send of a new chat the untitled resource is materialized into a fresh
real resource, so a new subscription is created at that moment and its
first read yields no customizations. Every migration candidate is then
filtered out and no hint is shown, even though the same computation
reports the correct counts once the snapshot lands.

Add whenCustomizationsReady so one-shot callers can distinguish 'not
loaded yet' from 'no customizations', and await it in provideSourceFolders.
The wait is bounded and cancellable because the chat request path blocks
on the hint before sending the user's message.

pull_requests.title: Fix Markdown code block editor iframe bootstrap
pull_requests.body:
## Summary
Fix resource loading in contributed Markdown code block editors by bootstrapping nested iframes through the permitted empty webview page.

- Use `/fake.html` instead of the outer webview's `/index.html`, retaining the webview origin and query parameters (including its ID).
- Update `@vscode/markdown-editor` from `0.0.2-88` to `0.0.2-90` with npm. The published package includes microsoft/vscode-packages#289, which forwards and stores the bootstrap URL all the way to the physical iframe.

## Why
The package previously dropped the URL, so frames fell back to `srcdoc` and the webview service worker could not associate their CSS/JS requests with a webview ID. Once forwarding was fixed, using `location.href` exposed a second issue: Electron's `isAllowedWebviewRequest` deliberately blocks nested requests to `/index.html` (`net::ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT`). `/fake.html` is already the supported empty bootstrap used by the webview wrapper. This change does not relax navigation security restrictions.

## Validation
- Verified npm version `0.0.2-90` has gitHead `7e778f85325333474d7b4d000e1ad2382e5a47b3` and inspected the installed published bundle for both constructor forwarding steps.
- `npm run compile` passed for the Markdown extension, including its webview, notebook, and Markdown editor bundles; extension TypeScript compilation reported zero errors.

pull_requests.body:
## Summary

- define VS Code-owned Codex permission profiles for Default and Auto-Review and apply them across thread starts, turns, forks, resumes, backing chats, multi-root workspaces, additional directories, and Agent Merge
- on macOS and Linux, deny arbitrary filesystem reads outside the active workspace roots while retaining Codex's required `:minimal` system/runtime reads and isolated temporary-directory access
- preserve Full Access as unrestricted, and keep additional writable directories separate from persisted workspace roots so clearing them revokes access
- describe Default and Auto-Review as platform-sandboxed rather than promising literal workspace-only reads

Fixes #334925

pull_requests.title: [cherry-pick] automations: fix: limit New badge to returning Agents users
pull_requests.body:
Cherry-pick of #334898 from `main`.

## Summary

Restrict the Automations **New** badge to returning Agents-window users with no prior Automation discovery, and stop treating loading or failed catalogues as proof that Automations are unused.

Follow-up to #334091. The badge designs and renderer already exist; this changes eligibility, lifecycle handling, and related tests.

Rebased onto `70a1d06d93f6a90d3cae4bf84754b096d818ef40`. The rebase reuses the canonical `catalogueState` API introduced by #334836 instead of retaining a parallel discovery contract. The PR now changes 15 files rather than 24.

## Why

The previous badge sampled the seen bit, definitions, and runs once, synchronously. If all were empty, it resolved the style and displayed **New**.

That causes two problems:

- A first-time Agents-window user sees a promotion even though the whole interface is new.
- Agent Host providers register and hydrate asynchronously. Empty arrays can mean "not loaded yet" or "unavailable", and the one-shot check deliberately ignored later definitions/runs. Unreadable legacy data can also produce an empty projection without establishing non-use.

## Implementation

### Returning-window detection without storage infrastructure changes

`SessionsWindowUsageService` snapshots whether the existing application-scoped, machine-targeted `agentSessions.telemetry.summary.appLaunchCount` was nonzero **before** recording the current open.

The first window therefore retains `hadPriorWindowOpen = false` even after it stores count 1. Later windows, including users whose count was written by older builds, are recognized without relying on chat/session history.

The usage service owns the increment; `SessionsLifecycleTracker` receives the captured count through `SessionsTelemetryContribution` rather than incrementing it a second time. The stored format and telemetry event schemas are unchanged, although the increment now occurs when the usage service is instantiated rather than specifically when the telemetry tracker is constructed.

This uses ordinary application storage. **No shared storage API, IPC, IndexedDB, or base/platform changes are included.** Two simultaneous first opens can both read zero and remain unbadged; that conservative false negative is acceptable for a discovery cue.

### Reuse upstream catalogue completeness

The badge reads the existing `IAutomationService.catalogueState` and accepts only `ready`. `loading`, `unavailable`, and `error` all suppress it.

Upstream already provides:

- Aggregation over registered provider stores **and the global legacy store**, with precedence `error > loading > unavailable > ready`.
- A loading guard until initial provider contributions settle, plus reactive updates for provider registration and catalogue changes.
- Observable legacy-ledger readability and Agent Host subscription health, without conflating those with migration authority.
- Conservative connection-state mapping: unsupported, disabled, and disconnected hosts remain unavailable unless their legacy storage reports an error.

The shared contract, aggregate and legacy implementations, Agent Host store implementations, provider interface, and architecture specification are unchanged from upstream. The former optional `initialDiscoveryState` API and its duplicated implementation are no longer part of this PR.

The local provider still needs the lifecycle fix: clear its connection listeners and Automation connection on host exit, then use its existing start binding to reconnect. This prevents a stale ready catalogue from surviving local host shutdown.

Migrated definitions and execution remain Agent Host-owned. Legacy ledgers remain compatibility sources; no schema, scheduling, permission, or session-template change is introduced.

### Conservative badge lifecycle

For an unseen returning user, the badge waits until `LifecyclePhase.Eventually`, then evaluates the current aggregate once. It shows only when the catalogue is ready and definitions/runs are empty. It does not await a retrying migration promise.

| Scenario | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| First Agents window | Hidden; no direct badge-style treatment request. |
| Returning user, ready and empty catalogue | Show the resolved style. |
| Existing definition/run or Automations view activation | Persist seen and hide. |
| Loading, unavailable, or errored catalogue at the startup decision | Suppress for that badge-state instance without recording seen. |
| Catalogue regresses after eligibility | Suppress; recovery does not automatically reveal it again. |
| Definition/run appears later, including through tools | Retire the badge and persist seen. |
| Developer reset | Explicitly preview despite prior-use/readiness/evidence gates, until Automations is activated. |

The startup phase is an opportunity for initial providers to populate, not a guarantee that every future provider has registered. The aggregate includes upstream's initial-provider-settlement guard; later data/readiness changes remain observable.

The existing hidden style setting, ExP styles, and accessible row labels are preserved. Style refreshes cannot bypass eligibility, and disposed states do not resume presentation after async work. The evidence observer is cleared on retirement.

## Scope and tradeoffs

- No new telemetry event or user-visible setting.
- No badge CSS, renderer redesign, or screenshot-baseline change.
- A slow, unsupported, unavailable, or errored source can hide the badge even for a user with no Automations; silence is preferred to a misleading promotion.
- Prior-use evidence is local application state, not account-wide adoption tracking. Historical view-only use before the seen bit existed cannot be reconstructed exactly.
- Startup suppression and developer preview are in-memory badge state; normal seen dismissal is persisted.

## Validation

After rebasing, using fresh transpiled output:

- **290 focused unit tests passed** across window usage, lifecycle tracker, telemetry contribution, badge, Sessions list, Agent Host Automation store, aggregate Automation service, and legacy Automation service, plus the targeted local host exit/restart regression.
- `npm run typecheck-client` passed.
- Targeted ESLint passed for all 15 changed TypeScript files; the final lifecycle-fixture adjustment was rechecked.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Verified zero diff from the new base for base/platform code, workbench storage services, generic fixture utilities, shared Automation contracts, aggregate/legacy implementations, Agent Host stores, and the architecture specification.
- Reviewed the rebase range-diff to confirm the prior-window snapshot, telemetry integration, and local-host cleanup were preserved.

The badge regressions cover all three non-ready catalogue states both at startup and after presentation, including recovery remaining quiet. The local-host regression starts with a completed catalogue and checks `ready -> unavailable -> ready` across exit/restart.

The earlier review concerns remain covered: unsupported hosts never imply a ready catalogue, and upstream now directly tests provider registration, live aggregate updates, startup settlement, and the full precedence matrix in both provider orders. This PR also checks aggregate `error` for a future-schema global legacy ledger.

Earlier validation exercised all 15 badge variants across Dark, Light, and Dark High Contrast. Visual fixtures were not rerun after this rebase; no visual styles or screenshot baselines changed.

To rerun the focused tests:

```sh
npm run transpile-client
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run src/vs/sessions/services/sessions/test/browser/sessionsWindowUsageService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsLifecycleTracker.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsTelemetry.contribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/automationsNewBadge.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/agentHostAutomationStore.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/providerAutomationService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/automations/test/browser/automationService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/test/browser/localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts \
  --grep '^(AutomationsNewBadgeState|SessionsWindowUsageService|SessionsLifecycleTracker|SessionsTelemetryContribution|Sessions - SessionsList|ProviderAutomationService|AutomationService|AgentHostAutomationStore|LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider Automation catalogue state follows)' \
  --reporter dot
```

For visual iteration in a development Agents window, **Developer: Reset Automations New Badge** force-previews the current `sessions.automations.newBadgeStyle` (`accent`, `soft`, or `outline`). Opening Automations dismisses it. This previews presentation, not production returning-user eligibility.
