pull_requests.title: Keep every pending steering message instead of only the last
pull_requests.body:
`ChatState` models the two pending-message kinds inconsistently:

```ts
steeringMessage?: PendingMessage;     // a single slot
queuedMessages?: PendingMessage[];    // a list
```

The `chat/pendingMessageSet` reducer follows suit, overwriting any existing steering message with no id check, three lines above a queued branch that correctly finds by id and updates or appends:

```ts
if (action.kind === PendingMessageKind.Steering) {
    return { ...state, steeringMessage: entry };
}
const existing = state.queuedMessages ?? [];
const idx = existing.findIndex(m => m.id === action.id);
...
```

### What a user sees

Send one steering message, then a second before the first is consumed, and the first one's bubble disappears from the sidebar. It comes back later, when the model actually picks it up and it lands in the transcript.

Nothing is lost, because the agent was handed the first message before the second arrived. What is lost is the pending state, so the UI stops showing work the user has already queued. The reappearance is what makes it confusing: the message looks dropped, then returns from nowhere.

Nothing in the UI required this. The pending-request projection already builds a list carrying a kind per entry, and pushed at most one steering entry only because the state could hold at most one.

### What this changes

`steeringMessages` becomes a list, and the queued branch is mirrored in the three reducer sites, the state aggregation, the pending-request reconciliation and the projection. The provider hook becomes `setPendingMessages(chat, steeringMessages, queuedMessages)`, and Claude, Copilot and Codex each loop instead of handling a single optional message.

### Relationship to #333919

`setPendingMessages` is a state sync, so the provider is re-handed whatever is pending on every pending-message change. #333919 fixes that re-delivery for the Claude path, in `ClaudeSdkPipeline`, clearing on consumption and on abort.

This change makes that fix matter more rather than less: where re-delivery previously repeated one message, it now repeats each message in the list. It deliberately does not add a second guard of its own, since #333919 already places one better than this layer could. If these land in either order the result is the same, but #333919 is the one that should land first.

### Testing

New test in `agentSideEffects.test.ts` covering the reported case: two steering messages, both surviving in state and both reaching the agent.

`agentSideEffects`, `chatContributions`, `sessionServerTools` and `claudeAgent` run 624 passing. Two failures in `agentSideEffects` (shell confirmation rules and shell-language forwarding) reproduce identically on unmodified `main` in the same environment and are unrelated to this change.

*AI disclosure: this comment and the related code were written with the assistance of AI.*

pull_requests.title: Report chat activity from the Claude agent session
pull_requests.body:
AHP already has a progress channel, and the workbench already renders it well. `chat/activityChanged` carries a human-readable string, and the client turns it into a shimmering row with a stable id, so each update replaces the previous row rather than stacking another one, and the row hides itself as soon as real content follows.

Nothing produces it for Claude sessions. The only producer anywhere in the agent host is worktree creation (`AgentService._resolveWorktreeBeforeSend`), which is why "Creating isolated worktree" is the only activity a user ever sees. Every other turn reports no liveness at all, so a session waiting on MCP startup, on model latency, or inside a long-running tool is indistinguishable on screen from a hung one. That window can be minutes, and there is nothing in the chat to say otherwise.

### What this changes

`ClaudeAgentSession` now reports on the activity channel:

- **on `send`**, because nothing reaches the SDK stream until the CLI is up, and that pre-stream window is the worst of the dead time
- **on each `ChatToolCallStart`**, naming the tool being run
- **cleared on turn complete, cancel and error**, so a finished turn cannot strand a stale row

Labels are deduplicated, so an unchanged one is not re-sent.

### Why the session and not the stream mapper

`claudeMapSessionEvents` is deliberately a pure SDK-to-signal mapping, and says so where the MCP contributor enrichment was kept out of it. Activity is presentation state derived from the stream rather than a mapping of any single SDK event, so it sits with the other session-owned enrichment (`_enrichSignalWithCredits`, `_enrichSignalWithMcpContributor`). Doing it in the mapper would also have prepended a signal to arrays that its tests assert on with `deepStrictEqual`, for no behavioural gain.

### Notes

No protocol change: the action, the reducer and the rendering all already exist and are unchanged. The Copilot and Codex providers are untouched, and could adopt the same reporting separately.

*AI disclosure: this comment and the related code were written with the assistance of AI.*

pull_requests.title: agentHost: preserve archived state in surfaced session notifications
pull_requests.body:
## Summary

Fix archived sessions reappearing in the Agents Window after an agent-host catalog rescan. A full listing applied persisted archive/read metadata, but subsequent `root/sessionAdded` notifications for the **same sessions** did not. The client accepted those notifications and displayed previously archived sessions as active.

This was observed after an Insiders update/restart: the initial catalog correctly contained **470 sessions with only 9 unarchived**, then the host replayed **254 existing archived sessions without their archive bit**. All 254 session databases still contained `isArchived=true`; this was an incorrect notification, not a permanent unarchive or recreation of the sessions.

## Incident timeline and retained evidence

Investigated a Windows update to `1.137.0-insider` on **2026-09-05**:

- Before: [b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698).
- After: [de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4), built on September 4.

The table uses **UTC throughout**. Main-process logs establish the update/restart; retained AHP JSONL transport logs establish the session-list and notification sequence. The plain agent-host log no longer retained the beginning of startup.

| Time (UTC, September 5) | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 09:39:57.086 | Last pre-update listing: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived. None of the unarchived sessions were last modified before August 15. |
| 09:40:53.341 | Update requested application quit/install. |
| 09:42:00.522 | Updated application started. |
| 09:42:08.851 | Another window subscribed to an unregistered `copilotcli:/untitled-...` session. |
| 09:42:31.584 | First post-update listing was still correct: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived; all 254 subsequently affected sessions were archived. |
| 09:42:32.389 to 09:42:36.383 | 254 `root/sessionAdded` notifications re-announced existing sessions with **status 33 instead of 97**. There were no new session IDs in this set. |
| 09:42:37.050 | The outstanding untitled-session subscription failed with `-32001`: `Session is not an adoptable legacy chat`. |
| 09:52:42.433 | A later full listing still reported all 254 affected sessions as archived. |

All 254 affected sessions were **created before August 15**; 249 were also **last modified before August 15**. Read-only inspection of their individual session databases found `isArchived='true'` and `isRead='true'` in **254/254**. There were no archive/unarchive commands in the three inspected startup client traces. The investigation did not modify user data.

### Relevant protocol excerpts

These are **redacted, pretty-printed field projections of actual JSONL records**, not complete payloads. Session URIs use stable placeholders; titles, prompts, project paths, working directories, connection IDs, and unrelated metadata are omitted. Full private log bundles are deliberately not attached.

**Another window -> host, 09:42:08.851Z** (that connection's line 30):

```json
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "subscribe",
  "params": { "channel": "copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>" },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:08.851Z", "dir": "c2s" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: initial list response, 09:42:31.584Z** (line 214; only one of the 470 items is shown):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "items": [{
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "status": 97,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-10T21:36:51.739Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-08-28T10:41:38.271Z"
    }]
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:31.584Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: notification for that same session, 09:42:32.389Z** (line 216, the first of the 254 notifications on lines 216-469):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "root/sessionAdded",
  "params": {
    "channel": "ahp-root://",
    "summary": {
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "provider": "copilotcli",
      "status": 33,
```

```json
  "error": {
    "code": -32001,
    "message": "Session is not an adoptable legacy chat: copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>"
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:37.050Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

The request/response correlation uses **connection + direction + request ID**, not request ID alone. This matters because the same connection can carry reverse-direction requests with reused numeric IDs.

The status difference is exactly the archive flag:

```text
97 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32) | IsArchived (64)
33 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32)
```

## Root cause

1. [The restore path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5168) receives the unregistered, non-adoptable untitled-session probe. Before treating absence as authoritative, it calls `awaitCatalogReadable()`, which requests a readable provider catalog with `requireReadableCatalog=true`.
2. That can force [the legacy catalog migration/rescan](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L1890), despite a persisted backfill marker. Registration is an UPSERT: success does **not** mean the session is new. Existing native sessions can therefore reach `_announceSurfacedSession`.
3. A session previously exposed by a full listing is not necessarily considered already *added*: [the state manager](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L880) separately tracks listed/published summaries and emitted add notifications. A correct initial listing consequently does not prevent this later announcement.
4. Before this fix, the announcement used provider metadata and forced the read bit, but **never overlaid persisted archive/read/title metadata**. Full listings did overlay it, explaining why the listings and database remained correct while the incremental notification was wrong.
5. [The Agents Window's notification handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L6055) updates an existing adapter from the incoming summary. Dropping `IsArchived` therefore resurfaces the old session. A request in another window can affect this window because they share the host.

The startup probe is present in the retained post-update trace and absent from the inspected first three minutes of the previous startup. The added regression reproduces the same **correct listing -> incorrect announcement -> correct listing/on-disk state** sequence using the public restore path.

## Fix

- Extract the full-listing metadata overlay into [a shared helper](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2119) and apply it [before incremental publication](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2739). Most production diff lines move the existing overlay rather than introduce a second implementation.
- Preserve persisted archive/read flags, custom titles, host-owned metadata, and changes summaries. Keep the legacy `isDone` fallback, with an explicit `isArchived` value taking precedence.
- Apply the legacy default-read behavior **before** the overlay, so an explicitly stored unread state is not overridden.
- Recheck visibility, tombstones, and live state after the asynchronous read. Continue filtering internal chat backings and dispose database references.
- If a metadata read throws, do not publish a guessed summary; release the announcement reservation so retry remains possible. Existing full-list error handling is unchanged.

This fixes the publication boundary rather than adding an age filter, suppressing every duplicate notification, changing migration defaults, or rewriting archived sessions. **No user-data repair is required.**

## Recent PR review / attribution limits

The investigation also reviewed relevant PRs merged in the preceding two days:

| PR | Merged (UTC) | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #334250 - workspace-less session conversion | September 4, 10:06 | No evidence establishes it as the cause of this notification bug. |
| #334518 - migration setting consolidation/default true | September 4, 15:53 | This is the installed tip, but this user's effective migration setting was already true before updating. |
| #332824 - auth replay/provider shutdown | September 3, 19:04 | A startup timing effect is possible but not established by the retained evidence. |
| #334449 - experiment defaults on assignment refetch | September 4, 10:41 | The logs do not support a migration-setting flip for this user. |

Both startups forwarded:

```json
{
  "migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled": true,
  "showExternalSessions": "recent"
}
```

The actual before/after build comparison found `_migrateLegacyProviderChats`, `_announceSurfacedSession`, `_surfacedSessionSummary`, `_awaitInitialProviderMigrationForProvider`, `_setupChatDiscoveryForProvider`, and the state-manager listing/announcement methods unchanged.

**Conclusion:** this is an existing catalog-publication bug exposed during this restart, not evidence that the update intentionally unarchived old sessions. The missing-draft probe/rescan is observed and reproducible; the retained evidence does **not** identify which recent PR, if any, caused that probe to occur.

## Regression coverage and validation

[Seven new regressions](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts#L4584) cover:

1. Archived sessions already returned by a listing, including their saved title.
2. Legacy `isDone` archive state.
3. An explicit restore taking precedence over legacy `isDone`.
4. Explicit unread state.
5. Legacy default-read behavior when no read metadata exists.
6. [The exact unknown-draft forced-rescan trigger](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentService.test.ts#L4660), starting with an archived registered session and a backfilled provider.
7. Metadata-read failure publishing nothing, followed by a successful retry.

All seven were run against the original production implementation and **failed before the fix**, then passed with the fix. In the exact-trigger case, the original implementation produced `before=[97], announced=[33], after=[97], persistedArchived='true'`; the fixed implementation produces `announced=[97]`.

Latest targeted aggregate/archive run: **110 passing, 11 existing skipped, 0 failing**. Fresh transpilation, changed-file hygiene (including ESLint), and patch whitespace validation passed.

```powershell
npm run transpile-client
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentService.test.ts --grep "aggregation|read/archive toggle|archiving an un-loaded|unarchiving an un-loaded"
npm run precommit -- src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\agentService.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentService.test.ts
git diff --check
```

<details>
<summary>Local full-build/type-check limitations (not reported as passing)</summary>

- `npm run compile-client` also compiles extensions; it stopped on missing `vscode-tas-client` declarations in the unchanged Microsoft Authentication extension.
- The narrower `npm run gulp compile-client` stopped because the checkout's generated `monaco.d.ts` was stale. Its generated-file changes were removed from this patch.
- `npm run typecheck-client` reported missing `electron` / `original-fs` declarations and diagnostics in unchanged Electron code. Neither changed file had a reported diagnostic, but the full type check is **not green**.

No unrelated source/dependency fixes or generated declarations are included. The PR changes only the agent service and its regression tests. CI Compile & Hygiene passes on the follow-up commit; the limitations above describe this local checkout.

</details>

## Review follow-up

Addressed the discovery-retry review in [bd9ded8ed0b](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/bd9ded8ed0b9f369757e47fdc7f065e91136d444). Discovery registers a session before announcing it, so simply releasing the announcement reservation on error was insufficient: subsequent discovery skipped the already-registered row.

Failed discovery announcements are now remembered independently of registration and retried on subsequent discovery, retaining the original external/native classification. The retry is claimed before awaiting so overlapping discoveries cannot discard it. Retrying does not re-register the row, reseed its read state, or add metadata reads to ordinary rediscovery.

Two additional regressions (nine new tests in total) cover host-created sessions reported as native or external, repeated metadata failures, concurrent rediscovery, successful recovery with stored archive/unread/title values intact, and deduplication afterward. Both additional tests fail on the previous PR head and pass with the follow-up. The review thread is resolved.

## CI follow-up

The original [Screenshots & Tests failure](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33974715903/job/101329283036) was only a blocking hash mismatch for `ResponsiveModelResizeCycleMinimal/Dark`. Image comparison found **10 rounded-corner pixels differing by one color level**, consistent with antialiasing noise; CI itself classified the visual delta as insignificant. All 15 fixture tests passed and 1,431 fixtures rendered without errors. Two subsequent successful main runs retained the committed hash.

No screenshot baselines were changed. The fresh [Component Fixtures run on the follow-up commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33976597591) **passed**, including the screenshot hash gate. The full [Code OSS workflow on the follow-up commit](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/33976597832) also **passed**, including Compile & Hygiene and the platform test matrix.

pull_requests.title: chat: mount MCP App webview in the window it is rendered in
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #331140

The root cause was already correctly identified by @kboyce-cloud in the issue report. This PR confirms that analysis independently, adds the ordering detail that makes a minimal fix sufficient, and applies it.

## Problem

An MCP App card (`ui://` resource, `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) renders blank when the chat is in an auxiliary window (`workbench.action.newChatWindow`). No app JS executes. Scrolling the card out of view and back makes it appear.

## Root cause

`ChatMcpAppModel` mounts its webview from the constructor:

```ts
const targetWindow = dom.getWindow(this._container);
this._webview.mountTo(this._container, targetWindow);
```

At that moment the container is still detached — `ChatMcpAppSubPart` builds `div.mcp-app-part` with `dom.$` and constructs the model before that node is inserted into the tree. `dom.getWindow` falls back to the element's `ownerDocument`, which is the main document, so `targetWindow` is the main window even when the card is being rendered into an auxiliary one.

`WebviewElement.mountTo` uses that window for three things: `_windowId`, the `parentOriginHash` input, and `_registerMessageHandler`. With the handler on the main window, the iframe's handshake `postMessage` (which goes to *its* parent, the auxiliary window) is never observed, the MessagePort is never established, and the queued `content` message carrying the app HTML is never delivered. Hence a blank card and no app JS.

The scroll workaround works because re-rendering routes through `onDidRemount` → `ChatMcpAppModel.remount()` → `reinitializeAfterDismount()`, which re-runs `mountTo(this.element.parentElement, getWindow(this.element))` with the element attached — and so reads the correct window.

## Fix

Defer the mount by one microtask and resolve the window then.

The issue notes that `reinitializeAfterDismount` already does the right thing; what makes a microtask sufficient — rather than an attach observer or post-attach callback plumbing — is that every caller attaches the container synchronously, in the same task that constructs the model:

- `chatListRenderer.ts` constructs the content part (~L2286) and appends `newPart.domNode` to the content container (~L2312) in one pass.
- `chatToolInvocationPart.ts` creates the sub-part and calls `appDomNode.replaceWith(this.mcpAppPart.value.domNode)` in the same autorun.
- `ListView.insertItemInDOM` inserts the row's `domNode` into `rowsContainer` *before* invoking `renderer.renderElement`, so the ancestor chain is already in the correct document during render.

By the time the microtask runs, the container is attached and `getWindow` reports the window the webview actually lives in. Nothing is lost by mounting a microtask later: `WebviewElement` queues `_send` calls while in the `Initializing` state, which is precisely the mechanism the existing `reinitializeAfterDismount` path relies on. If some future caller were to attach across an `await`, the microtask would resolve the main window — no worse than today, and still corrected by the existing remount paths.

Note the main-window case has the same ordering bug; it just happens to guess right, since the fallback window and the intended window coincide.

## What I verified, and what I did not

**Verified:** the bug reproduces on VS Code 1.136.1 stable with a remote HTTP MCP server serving an MCP App resource — renders in the sidebar and in an editor tab, blank in a new chat window, with only the iframe sandbox warning in the auxiliary window's console. The code paths and orderings described above were read against this commit.

**Not verified:** I was not able to build and run this patch. **The change is untested at runtime** — it is reasoned from the source, not observed working in a dev build. Please treat it accordingly; I'm happy to iterate if a maintainer can exercise it.

## Related, not addressed here

Two other sites resolve a window from a possibly-detached node and are likely to have the same latent problem. I left them out to keep this scoped to the reported bug:

- `chatMcpAppSubPart.ts` — `dom.getWindow(this.domNode)` is used for `innerHeight` (max webview height) and to register the `resize` listener, on the same detached node. In an auxiliary window this yields the main window's height and a listener on the wrong window. It degrades quietly rather than blanking.
- `chatOutputItemRenderer.ts` — `webview.mountTo(parent, getWindow(parent))` at render time, for `ChatToolOutputSubPart`. I could not construct a repro for this one, so I have not touched it.

pull_requests.title: Fix literal exclamation marks in gitignore patterns
pull_requests.body:
Fixes #334711

Ignore patterns containing a literal `!` can include or exclude the wrong file. With `*.txt` followed by `!important!.txt`, the shared parser currently re-includes `important.txt` and excludes `important!.txt`.

Recognize negation only at the start of a pattern, remove only that prefix, and unescape a leading `\!` when converting the remaining pattern to a glob. This also preserves negated character classes such as `[!a].txt`.

The parser is used by browser local-folder search and by Explorer when `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` is enabled. Existing rule-order and directory-traversal semantics are unchanged.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- 72 Electron unit tests passed across the ignore parser and glob suites, including 8 regression tests for literal exclamation marks, directories, negation, escaping, character classes, and case-insensitive matching.
- 27 file/directory/nested-path cases agree with `git check-ignore`; 17 of those cases disagree on the base revision.
- Client transpilation, changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` passed.

```sh
npm run transpile-client
scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/{workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile,base/test/common/glob}.test.js'
npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/ignoreFile.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile.test.ts
npm run precommit -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/ignoreFile.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/ignoreFile.test.ts
```

### Manual verification

The automated verification above exercises the core parser; the following UI checks have not been run:

1. Create `important!.txt`, `important.txt`, and `other.txt`, each containing the same search term.
2. Add a `.gitignore` containing `*.txt` followed by `!important!.txt`.
3. In browser local-folder search, keep ignore-file filtering enabled. Only `important!.txt` should contribute a search result.
4. In Explorer, enable `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`. With the fixture files closed in editors, only `important!.txt` should remain visible among the three text files.

pull_requests.title: Preserve literal dollars in case-converted search replacements
pull_requests.body:
Workspace Search reinterprets dollar sequences in case-converted captures as replacement syntax. Searching `^(foo.*)$` in `foo$1` and replacing with `\U$1` currently produces `FOOfoo$1`; this change produces `FOO$1` in both the preview and the saved file.

Fixes #334709.

Collect the converted capture separately and escape its literal dollars before appending it to the replacement template. Other capture substitutions continue through the existing path. Add seven regression cases covering capture references, whole-match/prefix/suffix references, escaped dollars, named-reference text, and mixed converted/unconverted captures.

Related to #299365 and #326451, which handle `$$` entered in the replacement field. That PR does not cover dollar sequences in case-converted captured text. This branch is based directly on `main` and does not depend on #334698.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- All seven new regression cases fail on the unmodified implementation and pass with this change.
- 258 related Electron unit tests pass; three existing/platform-specific tests are skipped.
- Changed-file ESLint, hygiene, and `git diff --check` pass.
- With fresh profiles and `--disable-extensions`, verified the Search view preview and actual Replace All edits in both baseline and fixed Code OSS: `foo$1`, `foo$&`, and `foo$$` now become `FOO$1`, `FOO$&`, and `FOO$$`.

```sh
scripts/test.sh --runGlob 'vs/{workbench/services/search,workbench/contrib/search,editor/contrib/find}/test/**/*.test.js'
npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/replace.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/replace.test.ts
npm run precommit -- src/vs/workbench/services/search/common/replace.ts src/vs/workbench/services/search/test/common/replace.test.ts
```

pull_requests.title: Fix search replacement case operations on short and empty captures
pull_requests.body:
Workspace search replacement can throw when stacked case modifiers outnumber the characters in a capture, and can insert literal case-modifier text when an optional capture is unmatched. For example, searching `^(?:([a-z]+)_)?([a-z]+)$` and replacing with `\u$1\u$2` changes `name` to `\uName` in the Search view, while editor find/replace correctly produces `Name`.

Fixes #334697.

Bound case operations by the capture length and treat existing empty or unmatched capture groups as empty strings. Preserve the existing handling of references to nonexistent groups. Add six regression cases for short captures, empty captures, optional groups, and subsequent groups.

### How to test

In **Replace in Files**, enable regex and leave **Preserve Case** off:

- In a saved file containing `user_name`, `name`, and `id` on separate lines, search `^(?:([a-z]+)_)?([a-z]+)$` and replace with `\u$1\u$2`. Both the preview and Replace All should produce `UserName`, `Name`, and `Id`.
- In a saved file containing `url`, `id`, and `x` on separate lines, search `^([a-z]{1,3})$` and replace with `\u\u\u$1`. Enable Match Case. Both the preview and Replace All should produce `URL`, `ID`, and `X` without an exception.

### Validation

On macOS arm64 with Node 24.18.0:

- 257 related Electron unit tests passed; 3 existing/platform-specific skips.
- 83 search integration tests passed.
- Client typecheck, changed-file ESLint, and hygiene passed.
- Reproduced the incorrect preview and actual file edits in installed VS Code 1.136.1. Verified correct preview and actual Replace All edits in a locally built Code OSS for optional captures and stacked modifiers on short captures.
- Full build passed after regeneration of a pre-existing stale `monaco.d.ts`; the unrelated generated change was restored and excluded, and the exact branch then passed client typecheck.

pull_requests.title: sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization
pull_requests.body:
## Why

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub items (assigned issues, authored PRs with conflicts / failing CI / unresolved review comments), falling back to standard options.

Analysis of experiment `f716301b` over 3 weeks and ~780k users found that, restricted to users with a resolved GitHub repository who saw the options widget (222,470 impressions):

- **61.0%** timed out with zero GitHub options
- **~9.4%** saw at least one GitHub option (only **0.17%** saw a full 3/3 set)
- **29.6%** got all-standard options

And we could not measure *how* badly, because `fallbackReason` was only set to `'none'` when all 3 slots were GitHub — so a widget with 2 real GitHub issues logged identically to one with zero. That blind spot covered 81% of impressions.

The root cause of the timeouts is that per-stage budgets could exceed the total budget: the PR chain was summary(5s) → review(4s) = 9s, with repository resolution also inside the same 10s budget.

## Telemetry

Additive only — existing field names and values are emitted in the same situations, so live dashboards keep working.

`onboarding.promptStrategy` gains:

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `gitHubOptionCount` | How many of the 3 slots were actually GitHub items — closes the main blind spot |
| `candidatesFound` | Pre-truncation count: "repo has nothing" vs "found items but were too slow" |
| `lookupDurationMs` | Total lookup time (plumbed from the value the code already computed for logging) |
| `repositoryMs`, `issueSummaryMs`, `issueLinkageMs`, `prSummaryMs`, `prReviewMs` | Which stage is actually slow |
| `issueSummaryOutcome`, `issueLinkageOutcome`, `prSummaryOutcome`, `prReviewOutcome` | Per-stage outcome, so "issues succeeded, PRs timed out" is distinguishable from total failure |
| `timedOutStage` | Which stage was in flight when the total budget expired |

`onboarding.promptOptionInteraction` gains `optionIndex` and `optionKindsShown`, making a true per-option CTR computable — today "implementFeature is most picked" is confounded with it being almost always present.

Both events gain a shared `impressionId`, so they can be joined per impression instead of on `DevDeviceId`, which is lossy for devices with multiple impressions.

Also splits the overloaded `noCandidate` — it meant both "no composer available" (an infra bug) and "lookup returned nothing" (a data outcome). The former is now `noComposer`.

**Privacy:** bounded categories and counts only. No issue/PR titles, URLs, numbers, repository names or prompt text. Every numeric has `isMeasurement: true`.

## Latency

`totalMs` stays at 10s.

1. **Publish issue candidates before linkage.** Linkage exists only to filter out issues that already have linked PRs, so a slow linkage call was discarding issues we already held.
2. **Review-thread enrichment off the critical path.** It fired N parallel lookups after a summary to produce `githubPRComments` — 30 selections, 0.37% of all picks — while `githubIssue` (the most-picked GitHub option) is the cheapest to fetch. The budget was being spent inversely to user value. It can now only refine, never delay first paint.
3. **Rebalanced sub-budgets** to `summaryMs: 4_000, linkageMs: 1_500, reviewMs: 3_000`. The issue and PR chains run concurrently under `Promise.all`, so the worst case for timed lookups is `max(4_000+1_500, 4_000+3_000) = 7_000ms`, leaving ~3s for repository resolution and rendering. Repository resolution has no budget of its own and a workspace change restarts the chain; both are bounded only by the `totalMs` race, and the comment on the constant says so rather than asserting a tighter bound than the code has.
4. **Streaming.** The 3 standard options are painted immediately and slots are replaced as GitHub items arrive, instead of blocking first paint on the whole lookup. Beyond timeouts, this also addresses V3's ~17pp tour-reach deficit versus V2.

## API change

`INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve` gains an optional progress callback:

```ts
export type NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress = (state: NewSessionPromptOptionsState) => boolean;

resolve(token: CancellationToken, progress?: NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress): Promise<NewSessionPromptOptionsState>;
```

Additive and optional, so existing callers are unaffected. It returns `boolean` rather than `void` deliberately: the composer refuses late updates while the user is already acting on the options, and the runner needs to know that so interaction telemetry describes what was actually rendered.

## Notes for reviewers

The streaming path has three subtle interactions that are each covered by a test that fails without its fix:

- `_renderedPromptOptions` is reset per `resolve`, not per `run`. `newChatWidget` calls `refreshPromptOptions()` on every workspace change against the same runner, and a per-run reset made the second refresh compare against the previous refresh's final set — suppressing first paint entirely in exactly the all-standard case this PR targets.
- `_promptOptionsSelected` is set at the *start* of `selectOption`, not in `onDidSelectOption`. The widget only reports a selection after the 2.5s prompt animation completes; a streamed update in that window would clear the selection and leave every option `aria-disabled`.
- The runner commits `_renderedPromptOptions` only when the composer accepted the update, so `optionIndex` / `optionKindsShown` can never describe options the user never saw.

`impressionId` is regenerated per `run`, not per `resolve`: strategy telemetry is emitted once per run, so a per-resolve id would orphan interaction events from any strategy event.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --grep "NewSession"` → **93 passing**, 0 failing
- `npm run typecheck-client` → clean for `sessions/contrib`
- `eslint` → clean
- Code hygiene → clean on changed files (the repo-wide `npm run hygiene` task fails on an unrelated pre-existing Windows path bug in `checkPackageJSON`, reproducible on an untouched checkout; no `package.json` is touched here)

New test coverage: partial GitHub candidate counts, the early issue publish, streaming updates arriving after first paint, budget-stage attribution, re-resolve after a workspace change, and the composer refusing late updates.

## Kusto queries this makes answerable

- Distribution of `gitHubOptionCount` (0/1/2/3) — the true personalization rate, vs today's binary
- Per-stage p50/p95 latency and timeout rate, attributing the 61% bucket to `repository` vs `prSummary` vs `prReview`
- `candidatesFound == 0` vs `candidatesFound > gitHubOptionCount` — "nothing to show" vs "found more than we could show"
- Partial-success cohorts, e.g. `issueSummaryOutcome == 'success' and prSummaryOutcome == 'timeout'`
- True per-option CTR, joining `optionKindsShown` impressions with `option` selections
- Position bias: selections by `optionIndex`, controlling for slot content
- Impression-level funnel joined on `impressionId`

### Validation

- All tests in the Copilot sessions provider suite passed (83 passing).

This fix resolves the error logged in the Insiders session and improves the handling of session change summaries. Other unrelated performance warnings were noted but not addressed in this PR.

pull_requests.title: fix: remove duplicate UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING import (build fix for vscode-engineering#3803)
pull_requests.body:
## Build failure

Every Compile task on `main` fails with `tsgo` TS2300 duplicate-identifier errors, cascading to all downstream Test/Publish/Verify jobs across the Linux, macOS, Windows and Quality stages:

```
src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts(33,10): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING'.
src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts(65,10): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING'.
src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts(47,10): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING'.
src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/copilotChatSessions/test/browser/copilotChatSessionsProvider.test.ts(64,10): error TS2300: Duplicate identifier 'UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING'.
Error: tsgo exited with code 1
```

## Root cause

`copilotChatSessionsProvider.ts` and its test each imported `UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING` from `../../../chat/common/constants.js` twice — once mid-import-block and once appended at the end of the import list. TypeScript rejects a symbol imported twice into the same module scope (TS2300), so compilation aborts before any task can run.

## How the fix works

Removes the redundant second `import { UNIFIED_WORKSPACE_PICKER_SETTING }` line in each of the two files, keeping a single import. The symbol is still available at all its use sites, so behavior is unchanged and typechecking passes.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Culprit: commit `291338d45a319004f26078f6b505745d62202f62` / PR #334674. A one-line duplicate-import deletion in each file lands faster and more safely than reverting a large model-picker PR touching many files. Owners to consult: `@lramos15`

## Validation

Verified by source inspection that only one import of the symbol remains in each file (`grep` count = 1). Full `tsgo`/compile validation could not be run in this environment; the change is a mechanical duplicate-import removal that directly resolves the TS2300 errors.

## Risk

Minimal — removes redundant imports only; no logic, telemetry, or runtime behavior changes.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@lramos15`

pull_requests.body:
Fixes #329065.

## Changes
- Add Copy Image, Save Media As, Open Source, and Reveal in Explorer View through the existing modal editor toolbar and an image-area context menu (including Shift+F10).
- Support Ctrl/Cmd+C without intercepting text input. Copy rasterizes to PNG. Save writes the cached preview bytes without additional re-encoding; web uses the existing download helper.
- Detect the actual encoded MIME for chat attachment bytes and correct the suggested export extension. Chat may already have resized/re-encoded an attachment (for example GIF to PNG), so exporting that preview does not reconstruct the original file or animation.
- Preserve real file/provider source URIs, excluding generated content, data identities, and pasted-image cache references.
- Open sources in the main editor group. Reveal uses the registered Explorer view in either workbench and suppresses auto-reveal during modal close/explicit selection, restoring its previous mode in finally.

## Review scope
No clipboard platform API, new service, editor-input selection model, CSS, settings, or accessibility-provider changes. Selection stays in the pane; the existing Blob cache retains the displayed bytes. Image signature detection is extracted from the existing base image helper and reused instead of duplicating parsers.

The optional Save As shortcut remains omitted because it conflicts with the modal keyboard guard. Save is keyboard-accessible through the standard toolbar/context menu without changing shared editor routing.

## Refresh and validation
- Merged upstream `main` at `a47dab6a0a5` without rewriting published commits (`93ea7d572a8`).
- Addressed all three review findings in `4ffc1202a0a`, with replies and resolved threads.
- Targeted Electron suites: **89 passing**.
- Targeted Chromium suites: **86 passing, 2 pending** (native Save dialog tests are Electron-only).
- Coverage includes actual GIF-to-PNG resizing, pasted cache provenance, encoded-format detection, corrected export filenames, and auto-reveal restoration on success and failure.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run transpile-client`, hygiene, and `git diff --check`: **passed**. The previous Sessions compile diagnostics are gone after syncing upstream.
- The complete Code OSS workflow passed on `4ffc1202a0a` after the upstream merge. The remaining fixture CI failure was reproduced locally and fixed in `c125969a43a` by reusing `registerWorkbenchServices` for the new carousel dependencies; all **8 carousel Playwright tests pass**. No screenshot baselines were changed. On final head `c125969a43a`, **Compile & Hygiene** and **Screenshots & Tests** both passed. The macOS Electron job failed an unrelated Agent Host Copilot cancellation/replacement-turn assertion (empty text instead of `replacement`); the same job passed on the preceding commit. Remaining jobs are finishing before an isolated retry can be requested.

issues.title: Outdated JSDoc on TextEditor.viewColumn ("when the editor column is larger than three")
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->
<!-- 🔎 Search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->
<!-- 🧪 Test using the latest Insiders build to see if your issue has already been fixed: https://code.visualstudio.com/insiders/ -->
<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.136.2 (and latest main)
- OS Version: Windows


Steps to Reproduce:

1. Inspect [`src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts#L1286-L1291) at lines 1286–1291.
2. The JSDoc for `TextEditor.viewColumn` states:
   ```typescript
   /**
    * The column in which this editor shows. Will be `undefined` in case this
    * isn't one of the main editors, e.g. an embedded editor, or when the editor
    * column is larger than three.
    */
   readonly viewColumn: ViewColumn | undefined;
   ```

---

### Why this is outdated:

1. **What the comment claims:** An editor column > 3 returns `undefined`.
2. **What the code actually does today:**
   In [`extHostTypeConverters.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTypeConverters.ts#L349-L355), `ViewColumn.to(position)` returns `position + 1` for any valid editor group column (`>= 0`):
   ```typescript
   export function to(position: EditorGroupColumn): vscode.ViewColumn {
       if (typeof position === 'number' && position >= 0) {
           return position + 1; // adjust to index (ViewColumn.ONE => 1)
       }

       throw new Error(`invalid 'EditorGroupColumn'`);
   }
   ```
   `ViewColumn` has since been expanded to include `Four` through `Nine`, and opening 4 or more editor groups in a grid returns the respective `ViewColumn` number (not `undefined`).
3. **When `TextEditor.viewColumn` is actually `undefined`:**
   It is only `undefined` when the editor is an embedded editor not placed in a main editor group (e.g. Peek Views, inline diff widgets, inline chat widgets).

---

### Historical Context:

1. **May 20, 2018 — PR #49599 ([commit `dd5afa5`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/dd5afa5bcc5263f62f66407fc8742bf59ee66b7c)):**
   When introducing Grid Editor Layout, the word `"three"` was initially removed from both `TextEditor.viewColumn` and `WebviewPanel.viewColumn`.
2. **May 22, 2018 — PR #49599 ([commit `0f8ef8c`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/0f8ef8cb0ae7654dda18794e1ced102353145e36)):**
   At that point in 2018, `ViewColumn` only defined `One`, `Two`, and `Three`. The runtime converter explicitly returned `undefined` for `position > 2`. `"or when the editor column is larger than three"` was added as a doc fix to document that temporary runtime limitation.
3. **June 2018 — Test Item #52315:**
   In the grid layout test plan ([#52315](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/52315)), the verification checklist explicitly verified:
   `[x] Verify textEditor.viewColumn is always defined for an editor in the grid even if many are opened`
4. **Subsequent updates:**
   `ViewColumn` was later expanded up to `Nine`, and the converter was made dynamic (`position + 1`). Other places like `WebviewPanel.viewColumn` remained clean (`"one of the editor view columns"`), but `TextEditor.viewColumn` retained this legacy note.

---

### Proposed Fix:

Remove `, or when the editor column is larger than three.` from `src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts`:

```diff
 		/**
 		 * The column in which this editor shows. Will be `undefined` in case this
-		 * isn't one of the main editors, e.g. an embedded editor, or when the editor
-		 * column is larger than three.
+		 * isn't one of the main editors, e.g. an embedded editor.
 		 */
 		readonly viewColumn: ViewColumn | undefined;
```

I would be happy to submit a PR for this change.

issues.title: Remote Agent Host customizations are incorrectly classified as user customizations
issues.body:
When using an Agent Host harness in a remote workspace, such as Remote WSL, workspace customizations discovered by the Agent Host are displayed under **User** instead of **Workspace** in the Chat Customizations editor.

For example, a workspace containing:

```text
.github/
├── copilot-instructions.md
└── instructions/
    └── test.instructions.md
```

shows both instruction files in the **User** section when the Copilot harness is selected. The same files are shown correctly under **Workspace** with a local harness.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a folder in a Remote WSL window.
2. Add a workspace instruction file such as:
   `.github/instructions/test.instructions.md`
3. Open Chat.
4. Start a new chat and select the Copilot/Agent Host harness.
5. Open **Chat Customizations**.
6. Inspect the **Workspace** and **User** sections.

### Expected behavior

The instruction is shown under **Workspace** because its file is contained by the current workspace folder.

### Actual behavior

The instruction is shown under **User**, while the Workspace section reports no instructions.

### Root cause

The remote Agent Host runs on the workspace side and discovers files using host-local URIs:

```text
file:///home/user/project/.github/instructions/test.instructions.md
```

The renderer receives workspace roots using workbench-side remote URIs:

```text
vscode-remote://wsl+ubuntu/home/user/project
```

The Agent Host protocol’s remote transport transforms working-directory URIs between these two representations, but it does not transform URIs contained in session customizations.

This leaves session state internally inconsistent: `workingDirectories` use `vscode-remote:` URIs while `customizations[].uri` and nested child URIs remain `file:` URIs. The customization provider’s URI containment check consequently determines that the discovered file is outside the workspace and classifies it as a user customization.

The affected transformation boundary is `EditorRemoteAgentHostTransport`.

### Proposed fix

Transform customization resource URIs at the remote Agent Host protocol boundary, using the existing `IURITransformer`.

The transformation should cover:

- Top-level customization source URIs
- Nested child customization URIs
- Customization icon URIs
- Workspace-scoped enablement URIs
- Client plugin child-enablement URIs
- Customizations carried in session snapshots
- `SessionCustomizationsChanged` actions
- `SessionCustomizationUpdated` actions
- `SessionCustomizationToggled` actions

The transformation must work in both directions and must leave opaque fields such as customization IDs, descriptions, and `_meta` values unchanged.

### Additional notes

This is a presentation/classification problem rather than a discovery problem. The Agent Host correctly discovers the workspace instructions; they are assigned to the wrong section after crossing the remote protocol boundary.

issues.title: Add Agents Window to the Windows taskbar jump list

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
## Feature request

Add an **Agents Window** task to the Windows taskbar jump list, alongside the existing **New Window** task.

Selecting it should launch VS Code with the existing `--agents` mode and open a new Agents Window. The task should use the branded Agents icon so it is visually distinct from a standard VS Code window.

## Motivation

The Agents Window is a top-level VS Code surface, but opening it currently requires first opening VS Code and invoking the command or keyboard shortcut. Adding it to the taskbar jump list makes it directly accessible from the Windows shell and keeps it consistent with the existing **New Window** entry.

## Proposed behavior

Under the taskbar jump list's **Tasks** section, show:

- New Window
- Agents Window, using the branded Agents icon

issues.title: Using /btw opens a split chat instead of the subchat treatment
issues.body:
### Description

When using `/btw` with the Copilot harness, VS Code opens a second chat side by side and reuses the loading indicator from the original chat. This is confusing because the new conversation appears related to the original chat, but is presented as a separate split chat.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a chat using the Copilot harness.
2. Run `/btw` while the chat is active.
3. Observe that a second chat opens beside the original chat and the original chat's loading indicator is reused.

### Expected Behavior

Present the `/btw` conversation using the same visual treatment as a subchat: tabs at the top and an indented child entry in the sessions list. If `/btw` is intentionally a separate chat at the SDK level, the UI should still make that relationship and loading state clear.

### Actual Behavior

Two chats are shown side by side, and the loading indicator appears on the original chat, making it unclear which conversation is active or processing.

issues.title: Agents window: Show confirmation after Commit and Sync actions complete

labels.name: feature-request
labels.description: Request for new features or functionality

issues.body:
## Feature request

In the Agents window, after I click the **Commit** or **Sync** button in the title bar, the button disappears. I assume this means the action completed successfully, but there is no clear confirmation of the resulting state of my changes.

## Current behavior

1. Open an agent session with changes ready to commit or sync.
2. Click **Commit** or **Sync** in the title bar.
3. The button disappears without an explicit success confirmation or an indication of the new repository state.

The disappearing button indirectly suggests success, but leaves uncertainty about whether the action completed and what state the changes are now in.

## Suggested behavior

After either action completes, show clear confirmation and the resulting state—for example, a brief success message and/or persistent status indicating that changes are committed, synced, or up to date. Failures should remain clearly distinguishable from successful completion. This doesn't need to be in a modal or anything the user needs to interact with or dismiss, but perhaps inline?

issues.title: Agent Host stops forwarding turn events after screenshot tool returns an image
issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Debug bundles are available privately on request; they may contain sensitive session data. -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Built-in Agent Host; Copilot runtime 1.0.84-canary.70.gdb75d0d.unsigned
- VS Code Version: 1.137.0-insider (645f29cc3176500b4b5762ba887cf2a7f0ffdf2c)
- OS Version: macOS, arm64
- Feature: Agents Window / Agent Host
- Selected model: GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Two Agent Host debug bundles captured; available privately on request

## Summary

After a browser `screenshotPage` tool successfully returns an image, Agent Host stops forwarding subsequent Copilot SDK events to AHP. The SDK continues running and completes the task, but the UI remains indefinitely on **Loading** because it never receives the later response parts or `chat/turnComplete`.

This has reproduced twice in the same session. The second capture is a clean reproduction with no steering, chat navigation, or subscription disposal.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host task that uses the integrated browser.
2. Have the agent call `screenshotPage` so the tool returns an image for model inspection.
3. Observe that the screenshot appears in the response.
4. Wait for the agent to continue.

## Expected

Events after the image-bearing tool result continue to stream to AHP. The UI shows subsequent progress/final response and receives `chat/turnComplete`.

## Actual

The screenshot tool completes and its image is shown, but the UI remains on **Loading**. Persisted SDK events prove that the agent continues through validation, commit, and a final answer. AHP emits no further response or lifecycle events for the request after the screenshot boundary.

## Correlated timeline from the clean reproduction

Pacific time, 2026-09-09:

- `08:35:40.588` — AHP delivers progress: `Reviewing catalog combination`.
- `08:35:41.495` — SDK starts `screenshotPage`.
- `08:35:41.576` — SDK records successful completion with a 59,939-byte JPEG asset.
- `08:35:41.578` — AHP delivers `chat/toolCallComplete` for the screenshot.
- `08:35:41.840` — AHP delivers the last observed `chat/usage` action.
- **AHP then emits no more response/tool/turn-completion actions for request `request_e29a7e78-0dc8-4095-9a2a-d9d3c55a0bb1`.**
- `08:35:41.728` — SDK ends the screenshot subturn and starts the next subturn.
- `08:35:53.111` — SDK sends further progress and starts final checks.
- `08:35:54.541` — checks complete successfully.
- `08:36:11.255` — commit completes successfully.
- `08:36:20.157` — SDK produces the final answer.
- `08:36:20.160` — SDK records the final turn ending.

The UI never receives these later events or `chat/turnComplete`.

## Secondary failure when steering the stuck turn

In an earlier reproduction, sending a steering message after the image stall cancelled the old request and released its buffered SDK events. Those old events were incorrectly attributed to the new AHP request, causing the new request to complete with the old answer. The actual new interaction was processed by the SDK, but its later AHP events had no request/turn ID and were effectively ignored by the UI.

This suggests two connected problems:

1. SDK-to-AHP event forwarding stalls after an image-bearing tool result.
2. Cancellation/steering after the stall can rebind buffered events to the wrong request.

## Notes

The clean reproduction rules out the model, screenshot generation, user steering, New Chat navigation, and early subscription disposal as the primary cause. The screenshot itself succeeds and reaches both the SDK and UI; forwarding fails immediately afterward.

issues.title: Copilot permissions cannot be revoked while running
issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 1.0.81-0
- VS Code Version: 1.136.1
- OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.22631
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Claude Opus 4.8
- Logs: Cannot be shared

If agent execution is started with "Autopilot" permission and then downgraded to "default permissions" while the execution is still in progress, the agent will continue to operate with autopilot permissions.

This is a commonly encountered scenario in the following workflow:
1. Create an execution plan in plan mode
2. leave plan mode using "Start Implementation with Autopilot"
3. Wait for agent to complete
4. Provide corrective feedback to agent
5. Realize that agent still has autopilot permissions from step 2
6. Revoke autopilot permissions
7. Agent keeps using autopilot permissions because it had them at step 5.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Have an agent running with "Autopilot" permissions on a difficult task where it would ask for clarification.
2. Change permissions to "Default Permissions" while the agent is thinking/considering.
3. Observe that question dialogs are "auto-replied with user is not available" e.g.:
> Q: What should "buildable on Windows" cover for this deliverable right now?
> A: The user is not available to respond and will review your work later. Work autonomously and make good decisions.

Workaround:

1. Explicitly fully stop execution. Tokens spent on incomplete work are lost.
2. Reset agent permissions
3. Re-prompt the agent including a notice that permissions have changed from what appears in repo/agent memories.

issues.title: Background subagent is not visible in the chat that spawned it
issues.body:
## Type of issue

Bug

## Description

When a chat starts a subagent through the background `task` mechanism, the subagent appears as a running item in the Sessions sidebar, but the chat that spawned it shows no persistent indication that a subagent is running. There is no visible status or link in the parent transcript that lets the user understand or navigate to the delegated work.

This is especially confusing when the parent chat is idle or appears complete while its delegated work is still running elsewhere.

## Expected behavior

The spawning chat should show a persistent, accessible representation of the background subagent, including its current status and a way to open it.

## Actual behavior

The background subagent is visible in the Sessions sidebar only. The parent chat does not expose it outside of the generic/collapsed task execution history.

## Notes

The existing Subagents pill derives its entries from tool-origin chats in the same session (`ChatOriginKind.Tool` with a matching `parentChat`). A background `task` subagent is represented as a separate agent session instead, so it does not enter that collection. The richer session-result link is also currently associated with completed `create_session`/`create_chat` tool calls carrying `sessionCreated` data, rather than the live background-task lifecycle.

@justschen I can share screenshots demonstrating the behavior with you in Slack; I have intentionally not attached them here.

labels.description: Issue identified as a duplicate of another issue(s)

issues.body:
Type: Bug Environment: VS Code 1.136.2, Remote-SSH to Linux x64, stock server install Symptom: Extension-contributed icon fonts render as tofu boxes in Remote-SSH windows (GitLens, CMake Tools). The same extensions render correctly in a local-folder window. Finding: every resource requested over vscode-managed-remote-resource fails, regardless of type. GET vscode-managed-remote-resource://window:N/…/eamodio.gitlens-19.1.0/dist/glicons.woff2 ?authority=ssh-remote%2B&scheme=vscode-remote → net::ERR_FAILED document.fonts reports error for every remote extension font; client-local fonts (codicon, seti) report loaded. Converting the font to .woff and repointing contributes.icons fails identically, so it is not format- or MIME-related. An Image() load of a URL taken verbatim from a VS Code-generated stylesheet rule (…/hbenl.vscode-test-explorer-2.22.1/icons/errored.svg) also fails. That file exists and is readable on the remote, so it is not a 404 or a permissions problem. Therefore not CORS either — image loads are not CORS-gated. Reproduction note: fetch() cannot be used to probe this scheme; the workbench CSP connect-src 'self' https: ws: refuses it and yields a misleading Failed to fetch. Use new Image(), and derive window:N from a live stylesheet rule, since the id changes on every reload and reconnect. Question for maintainers: is there a supported fallback to the HTTP vscode-remote-resource endpoint? That endpoint works correctly on this host (verified directly against the server socket), so a fallback would be a viable workaround. Separately, that endpoint's MIME table maps .woff but not .woff2, so .woff2 is served as text/plain; harmless before 1.135.0, but that release added X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff to the route, which would break .woff2 fonts for any client that does use it. issues.title: Feature request: Allow Copilot inline suggestions to use instruction files
issues.body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
Copilot inline suggestions should support a dedicated, opt-in instruction file for ghost text completions.

I am not asking for all existing chat or agent instruction files to be applied automatically to inline suggestions. That would likely add too much unrelated context and could hurt completion quality or latency.

Instead, there should be a separate instruction surface specifically for inline suggestions, for example:

* a dedicated workspace file for inline completions
* or a dedicated inline-suggestions section in existing customization files
* or a setting that explicitly opts selected instruction files into inline completions

Use case:
I work with a proprietary language for which the Copilot suggestions are not trained. This results in suggesting wrong operators, non-existing language features and functions.

Today, even if the workspace contains instructions that explain these rules, Copilot inline suggestions still propose JavaScript-like code in those embedded script fields (the proprietary language is vaguely similar to JavaScript). Chat can be guided by instructions and works well, but ghost text inline suggestions cannot.

Requested behavior:

* support an instruction file or configuration specifically for inline suggestions
* make it opt-in, not automatic for all instruction files
* allow teams to provide short, completion-focused rules for custom DSLs, embedded languages, or project-specific conventions
* scope it to the current file/language when possible

Why this would help:

* improves inline suggestions for custom DSLs and embedded languages
* avoids forcing all chat-oriented instructions into the inline completion prompt
* gives teams a focused way to steer ghost text behavior without overloading it
* reduces plausible-looking but invalid suggestions in domain-specific code

This request is specifically about ghost text / inline suggestions, not chat, inline chat, or BYOK/custom models.

issues.body:
Type: Bug 1. Create three custom chat modes (.agent.md) forming a nesting chain: A (root) -> B -> C, where A's allow-list permits calling B, and B's allow-list permits calling C. 2. Select A in the agent picker as the active chat mode. 3. Ask A to call B via the subagent tool. This succeeds (1 level deep). 4. Inside B, call C via the subagent tool (C is listed in B's own allow-list). This fails with: "Requested agent 'C' is not allowed by the current agent." 5. Confirm "Allow Invocations From Subagents" is enabled the whole time - toggling it has no effect on the result. 6. Add C to A's (the root's) allow-list too, then repeat step 4. Still fails with the same error, even though C is now listed in both A's and B's allow-lists. Result: any subagent call at nesting depth 3 or deeper is rejected, regardless of which agent's allow-list contains the target. This breaks coordinator -> worker -> specialist agent architectures, even though nested subagent calls and per-agent allow-lists both appear to be supported features. I believe the issue started around the 1.136.1 build because it worked about a week or two ago. issues.title: Side-by-side terminal layout is not restored when switching Agent sessions
issues.body:
Type: Bug

When multiple terminals belonging to an Agent session are arranged side by side, switching to another session in the Agents window and then switching back restores the terminal instances, but not their split layout.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open an Agent session in the Agents window.
2. Create at least two terminals for that session.
3. Arrange the terminals side by side using a split terminal layout.
4. Switch to a different Agent session in the Agents window.
5. Switch back to the original session.

## Expected behavior

The terminals and their side-by-side split layout are restored as they were before switching sessions.

## Actual behavior

The terminals are restored, but they are no longer shown side by side; the split layout is lost.

issues.title: Title bar "Layout Control" / action-toolbar-container icons don't use titleBar.activeForeground/inactiveForeground
issues.body:
**Versions**

- VS Code source referenced: [`main` @ 97be5ba](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/97be5ba242f0d03048aacb01f11bea8e3a2c264a)

## Summary

In the custom (non-native) title bar, several icon groups are not bound to the `titleBar.activeForeground` / `titleBar.inactiveForeground` color tokens, unlike the Command Center, the menubar (File/Edit/…) buttons, and the window controls (Windows/Linux), which all correctly pick up those tokens. This means any theme/extension that customizes `titleBar.activeForeground` via `workbench.colorCustomizations` only affects some of the title bar's icons — the rest silently keep the generic workbench foreground color and can end up low-contrast or mismatched against the customized title bar background.

## Repro / affected code

`src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/media/titlebarpart.css` ([current `main`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/97be5ba242f0d03048aacb01f11bea8e3a2c264a/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/media/titlebarpart.css)):

- Icons that **do** correctly bind to the title bar foreground tokens: the Command Center search box/icon and the menubar-menu-button rules use `color: var(--vscode-titleBar-activeForeground)` (and its `-inactiveForeground` sibling).
- The **Action Tool Bar Controls** group (rendered via `.action-toolbar-container`, populated from `MenuId.LayoutControlMenu` and `MenuId.TitleBar` in [`titlebarPart.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/97be5ba242f0d03048aacb01f11bea8e3a2c264a/src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/titlebar/titlebarPart.ts) — this is the Layout Control icon, the Accounts icon, and any editor actions relocated to the title bar via `workbench.editor.editorActionsLocation: titleBar`) instead has:
  ```css
  .monaco-workbench .part.titlebar > .titlebar-container > .titlebar-right > .action-toolbar-container .codicon {
    color: inherit;
  }
  ```
  There is no rule setting `color: var(--vscode-titleBar-activeForeground)` (or `-inactiveForeground`) anywhere for this container or its icons, so they fall back through `color: inherit` all the way to the workbench-wide `--vscode-foreground` token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Pick a dark color theme (e.g. any theme with light/white title bar icons by default).
2. Set a **light** custom `titleBar.activeBackground`/`titleBar.activeForeground` pair via `workbench.colorCustomizations` (or via an extension that does this, such as [Peacock](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=johnpapa.vscode-peacock) setting a light accent color) so that `titleBar.activeForeground` is computed to a dark color for contrast.
3. Observe: the Command Center and the menubar buttons all correctly render with the dark, customized foreground.
4. Observe: the Layout Control icon (and any other icon in the rightmost "action toolbar" group, e.g. Accounts) still renders in the theme's original light icon color, low-contrast against the light title bar background, instead of picking up `titleBar.activeForeground`.

## Expected behavior

All icons in the custom title bar — including the Layout Control / action-toolbar-container group — should consistently use `titleBar.activeForeground` / `titleBar.inactiveForeground`, the same way the Command Center and menubar icons already do, so that title bar contrast stays consistent for any theme or extension that customizes those tokens.

## Additional context

This was reported against the [Peacock](https://github.com/johnpapa/vscode-peacock) extension as [johnpapa/vscode-peacock#585](https://github.com/johnpapa/vscode-peacock/issues/585) (reported by @gdlx), where the observed symptom was that Peacock's title bar icon contrast handling appeared inconsistent with its activity bar handling. Investigation confirmed Peacock computes and sets `titleBar.activeForeground`/`titleBar.inactiveForeground` identically to how it computes `activityBar.foreground` (same shared contrast algorithm), and that the activity bar renders correctly — so the discrepancy is isolated to this specific VS Code CSS gap in the title bar's action-toolbar-container, not anything extension-side. Extensions like Peacock have no reachable, safely-scoped color-customization token to work around this from userland, since the only fallback token in play (`foreground`) is workbench-wide and would have far too broad a blast radius (editor/sidebar/panel text, etc.) to use as a substitute.

Happy to provide additional screenshots/repro if useful.

issues.title: GitHub Copilot: camelCase subagentStart hook is silently ignored
issues.body:
Type: Bug

## Description

In VS Code's native GitHub Copilot Chat extension, a GitHub Copilot hook using the documented camelCase event name `subagentStart` is silently ignored. The same hook works when its event name is changed to `SubagentStart`.

This is inconsistent with the GitHub Copilot hooks reference, which documents `subagentStart` as the event name. It is also inconsistent with other local Copilot surfaces: Copilot CLI and the VS Code Agents View accept both casings in my testing.

## Reproduction

1. In a workspace, configure a native GitHub Copilot hook in `.github/hooks/*.json` for `subagentStart`.
2. Enable `.github/hooks` as a hook location in VS Code's User settings.
3. Start a Copilot Chat session and delegate to a subagent.
4. Observe that the subagent runs but the hook command never executes; the Copilot Chat Hooks log contains no entry for it.
5. Change only the event key from `subagentStart` to `SubagentStart`.
6. Repeat step 3. The hook executes and its `additionalContext` reaches the subagent model.

## Expected behavior

The documented `subagentStart` event should be accepted, or VS Code should report an actionable validation error when it is not.

## Source-level cause

At commit `3e33b2105fb6e7feb2c2108c9074f66fac0b60f5`, the GitHub Copilot hook-name mapping omits `subagentStart` even though `vscode.ChatHookType.SubagentStart` exists:

- `HOOKS_BY_TARGET[Target.GitHubCopilot]` in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/hookTypes.ts`
- `HOOK_TYPE_MAP` in `src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/common/pluginParsers.ts`

`parseHooksJson` silently skips an unrecognized hook key. The second mapping has the same omission. Adding `subagentStart` → `SubagentStart` to both maps should restore the documented behavior.

The same source-level gap exists for `preCompact` / `PreCompact`; I have not separately executed a `preCompact` reproduction.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.136.1
- GitHub Copilot Chat 0.64.1
- Windows 11

References:
- https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/hooks-reference
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3e33b2105fb6e7feb2c2108c9074f66fac0b60f5/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/promptSyntax/hookTypes.ts#L36-L45
- https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/3e33b2105fb6e7feb2c2108c9074f66fac0b60f5/src/vs/platform/agentPlugins/common/pluginParsers.ts#L635-L654
